  Continue, the Tabs box and the ruler. Lists continue in flow order through cells, as Word numbers them
  (`ListRestart.listBefore`: Numbering on the paragraph after a table whose cells hold items 2 and 3 continues as 4;
  AutoList's "3. " after cells holding 1 and 2 continues their list; AutoList works in a cell, Tab still moving cells).
  Find / Replace / Replace all go through the paragraphs in flow order (cells row by row, cell by cell), wrap, and
  select the match in the cell (painted there as any text selection); matches are `{at, from, to}`. Bookmarks in cells
  are at their real places (added, found, gone to, deleted when they are inlines of their own); a mark between rows or
  cells is at a paragraph's edge (a row's or cell's lead: the start of its first paragraph; a row's or the table's
  tail: the end of the last cell's last paragraph) and cannot be moved or deleted. Links and pictures are inserted and
  edited in cells (paths), and found under the pointer there (`DocHit.leafAt`: a Ctrl-click on a link in a cell
  follows it; a picture in a cell is selected with its handles at the cell's x and resized). Word count counts a
  selection's blocks at every depth (`SelShape.covered`: a `cells` rectangle its cells). Insert > Page break and
  Section break are shaded with an end of the selection in a cell (`InsertApply.breakable`; their keys beep, C3.4).
  An inserted picture (Insert > Picture..., a drop, a pasted image: `PicLoad`) is sized to the cell's text width since
  the C3 fix wave (`InsertPicture.insert` with the window's layout: the cell's column, the innermost cell's), so the
  file holds the size it is drawn at; resizing it by its handles and its alt text work in a cell as anywhere (checked
  by `word-tables-edit` and `cellformat`). Costs on 50,000 paragraphs (median of 21): `touched` of the whole document 1.4 -> 3.7 ms,
  `Format.query` at a caret 0.3 -> 0.5 ms, a selection's word count 4.2 -> 6.1 ms, Find through the whole document
  without a match 2.8 -> 3.0 ms.

* **User guide (C2.6):** part 10 of `$.Docs.Letters`, "Tables" (what is shown, what is kept but not shown, the grey box that
  remains for tables the reader cannot model, selecting and deleting, "editing arrives in the next steps", and what is
  still to be checked in real Word: TB3, TB4, TB7). Parts 2, 7, 13 (What is kept), 17 (What is coming) and 19 (Things
  to know), `tools/docs/Contents`, `!Help` and the README no longer call tables a grey box except for the Opaque ones.
  C3..C7 extend part 10 as editing arrives; nothing in it describes editing. C2 fix wave: part 10's widths (the
  window scrolls to a table's right edge; beyond the page it is on the grey desk) and cell text (its list numbers
  and pictures: `word-tables` checks both by pixels); part 9 no longer says pictures in tables are not shown (they
  are, but cannot be selected yet), and a table holding a picture comes whole within one document (as text in
  another); part 3's word count: a table's lines are not counted yet (`WordCount` counts top-level lines only; since
  the C3 fix wave they are, and the guide says so).

* **User guide (C3.6):** part 10 of `$.Docs.Letters` now has "Working in a table's cells" (caret, arrows, Tab, Shift-Tab,
  Ctrl-Tab, Enter), "Selecting cells" (drag, Shift-click and arrows, the cell, row and column zones), "Typing and
  deleting in cells" (clearing, removing rows, TB10's edges, bookmarks, Ctrl-Enter refused) and "Formatting, lists,
  links and the rest in cells"; parts 2, 3, 4, 8, 9, 17 and 19, `tools/docs/Contents`, `!Help` and the README no longer say
  the caret cannot enter a table, text in tables is not searched, or pictures in cells cannot be selected. The "still
  to be checked in real Word" paragraph lists what is unverified: marks of deleted rows, a mixed range's paragraph
  formatting, where marks between rows and cells are shown, a picture's size in a cell, Ctrl-Tab. Not yet claimed in
  the guide: resizing a picture in a cell, copying cells (C6).
* **User guide (C5.5):** part 10 of `$.Docs.Letters` gained "Table properties" (the box's nine fields, the 0.02..22 in
  limits, never rounded, what an empty field means, Cell alignment), "Lines and shading of cells and tables" (Apply to
  Cell / Table, the neighbouring cells, Fill None, the raw refusals), "Dragging the edges of columns and rows" and "The
  ruler in a table", and a C5 "still to be checked in real Word" paragraph (TBC5a..o); part 6's Borders and shading
  points at it; parts 1, 17 and 18's lists, `Contents`, `!Help` and the README no longer say table width, lines and
  shading cannot be changed (not yet: Convert, copying cells: C6). No part moved.
* **User guide (C6.5):** part 10 of `$.Docs.Letters` gained "Copying and pasting tables" (what a cell rectangle, rows,
  a whole table and a mixed range copy; where a table goes: in text, in a cell nested to depth 8 then as text, over
  cells overwriting them; table styles copied across documents), "Tables and other programs" (HTML and tab text out;
  HTML tables in, the 63 / 1000 / 8 / 63,000 limits, flattened beyond), "Converting text to a table and back" (both
  boxes, the separator rules, what is refused) and a "still to be checked in real Word" paragraph (TBC6a..k); the
  Table menu listing gained Convert >. Part 4 (copying within and across documents, what other programs get and
  take, "Not possible yet"), part 9 (a table with a picture comes whole across documents), parts 17 and 19, the
  guide's opening paragraph, `Contents`, `!Help` and the README no longer say tables come as text or cells cannot be
  copied. Part numbers did not change.
* **User guide (C5 fix wave):** part 10's "Table properties" says a percentage width opens with Table width empty and
  the field greyed (Auto or Length first; the "Choose Auto or Length..." refusal) and that lengths are compared as
  shown; "Lines and shading of cells and tables" gives the new neighbour rule (a line put on: the selected cells only;
  taken off: also the cells along the edge, not a wider one, none with cell spacing; a line only the neighbour draws
  shows off; Table keeps the cells' own lines) and the message line; "Dragging the edges" the 0.01 in least row
  height, no row drag inside a merged cell, a style's width made the table's own, the nearer of nested and outer
  lines, the right-edge line for centred tables, a window closed mid-drag; the real-Word paragraph TBC5h, q, r. The
  README's Formatting tables paragraph and `!Help` follow.
* **User guide (C3 fix wave):** part 3 (a bookmark mark in a paragraph Backspace or Delete removes beside a table is
  kept; the word count's lines include table cells), part 10 (the arrows never stop in a vertical merge's hidden
  lower parts; a table whose cell ends with another table stays a grey box; a cell always ends with a paragraph;
  a picture put in a cell is made no wider than the cell, resized and given alt text there as anywhere; still to be
  checked: whether Word sizes it to exactly the cell's text width) and part 13; `!Help` and the README feature text
  the same (the "a picture put in a cell is sized to the column" limit is gone).
* **User guide (C7.3):** part 10 of `$.Docs.Letters` gained "Keys in tables, at a glance", "Limits", "What is kept,
  untouched, in a table" and "Not possible yet"; part 17 (What is coming) lists the table items; the `!Help` and the
  README carry the limits and the list of what is not possible yet. Every "part N" pointer was checked.
* **Ctrl-Tab in a real browser (C3.3, R21).** Chrome, Firefox and Safari keep Ctrl-Tab for their own tabs, so the key
  that types a tab in a cell (`Keymap` `cellTab`) may never reach the page (the browser suite cannot see this). The
  guide says so. The Table menu step (C4) is to give the same action a menu route.

### Hostile input and speed (C7.1)

* **The suite.** `tests/moreapps/word-tables-hostile.mjs` (browser; `SECTIONS=hostile,big,budgets,ops,convert,random,close`
  runs only some; about 80 s): D14f's set opened in the window (10,000 rows, 63 and 64 columns, `gridSpan` 0 / 64 / -1 /
  1e9 / x, an empty and a 0-width grid, a `vMerge` continue first, depth 9, ragged rows, a row of only marks,
  `__proto__` names), each typed or Opaque as expected with no message, laid out, drawn, edited and undone to the opened
  model. Refused with a message, in under 10 s, the window still usable: a file of 1,008,000 cells and one of
  1,000,001 paragraphs in cells (both stopped by the window's 200,000-paragraph cap, which the window words as "it has
  more than 200,000 paragraphs, the most !Letters opens": `DocxError` kind `paragraphs`, C7 fix A4), and 200 nested tables (the XML parser's depth
  cap: "not well-formed"). Then 1000 x 5, 1000 x 63, a merged staircase, a table with every column merged top to
  bottom, depth 8 and 100 tables opened and scrolled end to end; keystrokes, a drag across cells and the first arrow
  press across 4995 hidden cells measured against the same operation in a table-free document of the same run (ratios
  and margins, never a bare threshold); select all + Delete and undo; 1000 Tab presses at the last cell (the caret put
  at the last cell before each: the Tab key in a 5-column table adds a row only every fifth press) and undo of all 1000
  steps (about 10 s); Table to text and Text to table over 5000 and 63,000 cells; hostile HTML tables pasted; column
  borders dragged; 500 seeded random actions (the page's own choices come from a seeded generator, so a run repeats);
  windows closed mid-drag, with each box and a menu open, and 20 open / close cycles.
* **Measured (this machine, key handler + layout + paint, median of 25 presses, milliseconds):**

  | key | 1000 x 5 cell | table-free, 5000 paragraphs | 1000 x 63 cell | table-free, 63,000 paragraphs |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | type | 0.4 | 0.2 | 2.2 | 0.2 |
  | Backspace | 0.5 | 0.3 | 2.3 | 0.8 |
  | Tab / ArrowRight | 0.5 | 0.5 | 2.2 | 0.4 |
  | Shift+ArrowRight | 0.5 | 0.3 | 2.1 | 0.3 |
  | Ctrl-B on a paragraph | 0.8 | 0.4 | 2.5 | 3 |

  The first ArrowRight after an edit across 4995 hidden cells of a 1000 x 5 table with every column merged top to
  bottom: 1.3 ms (107-175 ms before `SelVert` marked hidden columns once per layout; 3.2 s at 1000 x 63). Opening: 1000 x
  5 about 0.1 s, 1000 x 63 about 1.1 s, the merged staircase 1.2 s. Table to text / Text to table: 1000 x 5 85 / 133 ms,
  1000 x 63 209 / 1088 ms (63,000 cells). A 30 px column drag releases in 8 ms (1000 x 5) and 0.4 s (1000 x 63).
* **The 50,000-paragraph document (the +5 ms budget, D20).** `tests/moreapps/relayout-perf.test.mjs` times the relayout
  after one edit (the keystroke's work, median of 25) and fails only on a gross regression (above 25 ms) or on
  non-linear growth. The comparison with the main branch before Batch C was made by hand in the same session, six
  interleaved runs each: main (Batch B) 9.3-10.1 ms, this branch 12.2-14.4 ms, so +2.9 to +4.4 ms (the C2.1 report
  said +0.8 then; the cost is the per-item fields `x`, `w`, `col`, `ci`, the `L.flow` array and the garbage they make:
  in a CPU profile `itemOf` is 1231 ms against `buildItems` 919 ms over 150 relayouts, the collector 302 against 109).
  It was inside the +5 ms budget with about 1 ms to spare. **C7 fix A3** (target: within +2 ms of main): a table-free
  layout no longer pays for tables: `L.flow` is made only at the first table (before, a second 50,000-entry array was
  built and dropped), a paragraph's item is built by `DocItems.paraItem` (no table checks, `ci` in the literal instead
  of a later write), `ry` is set only on items in cells (it added a property to every item), and `invalidate()` skips
  the `byId` pass. Measured again, six interleaved runs each: relayout main 9.2-9.8 ms, this branch 9.7-10.5 ms (-0.1
  to +1.2 ms); a whole keystroke (`Typing.type`, the relayout and `Selection.clamp`, median of 40) main 12.8-13.5 ms,
  this branch 11.6-12.3 ms. What remains of the difference is the four column fields every item still carries (`x`,
  `w`, `col`, `ci`; the C2 design: items are placed by their column): an experiment without `x`, `w`, `ci` gave
  about 0.5 ms more, but every reader (`DocPaint`, `DocRects`, `DocHit`, the decorators, about 20 modules) would need a
  fallback to the page, a design change not worth it inside the budget. The browser suites' 50,000-paragraph budgets
  (`word-typing-hostile.mjs`, `word-format-hostile.mjs`) pass unchanged.
* **Batch D P2.3 (`dirtyFrom`, D37: Draft within +5 ms of main).** `relayout-perf.test.mjs`, three interleaved runs
  each, the same session: main (6f1e8192, exported with `git archive`) 10.69, 10.82, 10.79 ms; this branch before
  P2.3 (f1fcff82) 10.51, 11.07, 10.60 ms; with P2.3 12.30, 12.20, 12.90 ms: +1.4 to +2.2 ms against main, inside
  the budget. The P2.3 work per relayout is a few compares per root item (`ItemReuse.track`, the gaps of
  re-decorated items in `DocStack`) and one array of section props; a direct timing of the same relayout (median of
  55, three runs) gave 10.96-11.48 ms with P2.3 against 10.60-11.39 without, and the repository tree with the P2.3
  layout files reverted measured 11.5-11.9 ms in `relayout-perf`, so about 1 ms of the difference is not the code.
* **Batch D P5.1 (D37: Draft within +5 ms of main, measured again).** `relayout-perf.test.mjs`, three interleaved
  runs each, the same session: main (6f1e8192, `git archive` of `origin/main` into the scratchpad) 9.38, 9.26,
  9.51 ms; this branch (7600311d + P5.1, which changes no layout code) 9.84, 9.98, 9.96 ms: +0.3 to +0.7 ms against
  main, inside the budget (P2.3's +1.4 to +2.2 ms was measured on a busier machine). The Print layout budgets are
  asserted by `pages-perf.test.mjs` (fixed ceilings, medians of 21 after 3 warm-ups, the 50,000-paragraph document
  at 800 px, 1,667 pages, fake measurer): opening's full pagination (galleyOf, Pages, PlacePrint, finish) 36-39 ms
  (ceiling 150); a convergent keystroke on page 833, relayout + new Pages from the last + the caret's page, 11.0 ms
  against Draft's relayout 9.8 ms in the same run (ceiling Draft + 5; one slice then finishes it); a line added at
  the top, the first pages 0.08 ms (ceiling 5) and every page 35-40 ms in 2 ms slices (ceiling 300), the same pages
  as a fresh pagination; painting a 1000 px screen at page 833 with `paintView`, before and after a keystroke,
  builds the frames of 2 pages at most. With page reuse switched off the keystroke test fails (31 ms; not converged).
* **Batch D P8.3 (fields shown computed; D37: Draft within +5 ms of main).** `relayout-perf.test.mjs`, three
  interleaved runs each, the same session: main at the rename (06c45a52, `git archive` into the scratchpad) 9.70,
  10.09, 9.87 ms; this branch with P8.3 10.59, 10.36, 10.30 ms: +0.4 to +0.9 ms, inside the budget. Against the
  branch before P8.3 (5c7d5a5c) 10.14, 10.20, 10.16 ms -> 10.39, 10.24, 10.18 ms: the field work is not in a
  keystroke without fields (one `localName` per U+FFFC in the paragraph laid out, no field code). `pages-perf`'s
  keystroke budget is now the median of the paired differences (each Print layout run less the Draft run just
  before it), best of three attempts: it failed now and then under the parallel unit run (+5.8 to +8.6 ms against
  +3 alone) because the two medians were taken over different moments of the machine's load; a real 5 ms cost is
  in every pair of every attempt, so the check guards the same thing (measured 2.5-2.8 ms).
* **Batch D P14.1 (D37 re-run at the end of the layout extras: Draft within +5 ms of main).** `relayout-perf.test.mjs`,
  three interleaved runs each, the same session: main at the rename (06c45a52, `git archive` into the scratchpad)
  10.32, 10.23, 10.24 ms; this branch (after P13.4 and the P14.1 fixes) 11.73, 12.42, 12.11 ms: +1.4 to +2.2 ms
  against main, inside the budget (P8.3's +0.4 to +0.9 ms; columns, line numbers, floats, wrap and the views add
  their checks to every relayout). The other D37 budgets, all passing: `pages-perf.test.mjs` (1,667 pages) open
  53.6-57.9 ms (ceiling 150), a convergent keystroke paired difference 3.2-4.2 ms (ceiling 5), a line at the top
  0.11-0.15 ms for the first pages (5) and 52.9-59.5 ms for all (300); `lineshape.test.mjs` 100 pages with a float
  on every page, a keystroke beside a float median 2.82 ms and in a floating table's cell 2.74 ms (ceiling 30);
  `linenumbers-perf.test.mjs` a keystroke on page ~800 adds at most 1 ms (first `numbersOf` 0.05-0.08 ms).
* **Found by the suite.** A table whose layout measures text while the window is being made (a grid of zero widths,
  any autofit table whose cells need more than the grid gives) failed to open with "Cannot set properties of null
  (setting 'font')": `DocWindow.metrics()` measured on the window's canvas before it existed. It now measures on a
  scratch canvas until then (`AppWin`, tested in `word-tables.mjs`).
* **Whole corpus.** `WORD_EDIT_CORPUS=1 NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096 node --test tests/moreapps/tables-roundtrip.test.mjs`:
  139 corpus files hold a table; 138 read (the one refused is the file `corpus-expected.json` lists), 0 failures, in
  77 s: 30 random document ops and, in a second run, 30 random table commands (every `TABLE` id, Split cells, Table
  properties and Borders patches, Insert table, text <-> table; hostile arguments count as refusals) per file, each
  written, read back equal, linted, xmllint-checked and undone to the opened bytes; the second generation of every file
  is byte-stable. The Opaque-reason histogram stays pinned by `tables-corpus.test.mjs` (`corpus-expected.json`
  `opaqueTables`).

### The rules R1..R24 as finally implemented

The plan's rulings, reconciled with the code and the ledger at the end of Batch C (the sections above say how each
works; this is the one list). "Retired" means a stop-gap that a later task removed.

| rule | as implemented |
|---|---|
| R1 | `corpus-expected.json` holds `opaqueTables`, an OBJECT reason -> count; `corpus.test.mjs` and `roundtrip-lib.mjs` skip non-string entries; `tables-corpus.test.mjs` asserts the histogram EQUALS it (every reason of R3, 0 where the corpus has none; `tail` is 0). Any change is a reviewed change of the pin. |
| R2 | Structural values fail closed: `gridCol w:w` an integer 0..31680 spelled as the writer writes it, 1..63 grid columns, `gridSpan` 1..63, `vMerge` absent / restart / continue / bare, `gridBefore` / `gridAfter` 0..63, a row's `gridBefore` + spans + `gridAfter` <= 63 (reason `span`), no `hMerge`. Display fields not understood go to `extra`. |

| R4 | `TblRead.MARKS` (bookmarks, comment and permission ranges, `proofErr`, move ranges) may sit between rows and cells (a row's or cell's `lead`, a `tail`); directly in a `w:tc` they are an Opaque cell block. |

Rulings of the final fix wave (after the whole-branch review):

* **Table to text keeps the file's order (final-1 M2).** With a separator a cell's paragraphs stay together and in
  order (`TblToText`), so text and bookmark marks never reorder; TB16 and TBC6k still ask what Word does.
* **A reversed pair is put right by moving its END (final-1 I2).** `TblPairs.endsAfter`: the bookmark becomes empty
  at its start, never longer (`inOrder`, for merges, moves the start instead, as before).
* **Grids are held weakly (final-2 I3).** Fixed, not parked: the change was small (`TblGrid`). The undo history still
  keeps each old table version itself (rows shared where unchanged), as it must to undo; a command that copies every
  paragraph (select all + bold on 63,000 cells) costs its copies per step, as in a table-free document.
* **The final-2 minors M1-M7 and M9-M12 are known limits** (the guide's part 10 says them where users meet them; the
  list is under "Known limitations of tables, consolidated"); M8 (the Tab item) was fixed.

### Known limitations of tables, consolidated

Each is described where it arose (the section named); this is the list to read first.

* **Not built (the guide's "Not possible yet"):** (pages came in Batch D: rows split and header rows repeat in Print
  layout, "Tables across pages" below; so did floating tables placed on their page with text flowing round them, in
  Print layout only, owner ruling R5: "Floating tables placed" and the P12b fix wave below; Draft, Web layout,
  Outline and a floating table in a cell, a header or a footer keep it in the flow with the dashed outline) moving
  a floating table by dragging (its edges drag; `tblpPr` never changes), tracked changes to a table (the table stays
  Opaque; !Letters has no Track changes switch), editing or making a table style, AutoFit commands, sorting, formulas,
  `textDirection` and `bidiVisual` (kept, drawn left to right), content controls round rows or cells (Opaque, reason
  `wrapped`).
* **Opaque on purpose:** the reasons of R3; tracked changes INSIDE cell paragraphs type, as in the body (owner to
  confirm); a cell ending with a table stays Opaque (`tail`).
* **Hidden text of a vertical merge:** Find, Replace and Go to reach it (TBX1); the hidden cells are skipped by the
  arrows and clicks.
* **Bookmarks:** the rules above ("Bookmarks and table deletions", "Table structure commands"); a bookmark END in a
  merged cell's lead is emptied by a merge (N1); a cut and paste inside one document drops bookmarks and comment
  ranges; Insert > Bookmark... with a cell rectangle marks from its first cell to its last in reading order, cells
  outside the rectangle between them included (Word would use `colFirst` / `colLast`: final-2 M9).
* **On screen (final-2 minors, parked):** fills are rounded to layout pixels, so 1 px light seams show between shaded
  cells at 50, 75, 90, 110, 125, 150 and 175% (`TablePaint` `fill`, M1); 0.5 pt single borders are anti-aliased to
  grey below 100% (`BorderPaint`, shared with paragraph borders, M2); the caret and the selection rects are not
  clipped to an exact-height (clipped) cell (`DocHit`, `DocRects`, M3); `SelTable`'s `CELL_EDGE` (4) and `ROW_ZONE`
  (24) are layout pixels, so the zones scale with the zoom while `TblEdge`'s drag zone is 3 screen px (M4); a press
  just right of a border selects the cell's content, which stays after the drag (documented, M5); undo of a column
  command puts the caret in row 0 (R18) and undo of a merge restores a caret, not the rectangle (by design, M6); a
  nested table wider than its cell has no drag zones outside the outer cell (C5 M1, M7).
* **Keys and boxes (final-2 minors, parked):** Convert's Other separator cannot be a space (WimpLib `readField` reads
  whitespace-only text as empty; Word allows one, M10); on a Mac Split table is Ctrl+Shift+Enter and Cmd+Shift+Enter
  makes a line break (the "Ctrl on a Mac too" rule, M11).
* **Clipboard and conversion:** the 100,000-block / 5,000,000-unit store bound, the HTML limits (R16), Strict
  spellings of a pasted Transitional table, content controls left out across documents, Table to text converts the
  whole innermost table (TBC6h).
* **Drags:** a pointer-cancel puts a drag's change in (the core's `wimp.drag` has no cancel event: `docs/CHANGES_NEEDED.md`);
  the dashed line of a centred table's right edge is approximate (TBX3).
* **Keys:** Ctrl-Tab is reserved by Chrome, Firefox and Safari: the Tab menu item is the route (`docs/CHANGES_NEEDED.md`).
* **Widths:** colour of themed table styles is the literal colour (TB4b); the autofit width of a table is estimated
  (TB7); `wBefore` / `wAfter` are kept as they are when `gridBefore` / `gridAfter` change.
* **Pre-existing, owner to decide:** a literal tab inside one `w:t` is not counted by the word count ("Known items from
  C1"); row-level content controls (13 rows, 16 cells in the corpus's 12 `wrapped` tables) keep their tables Opaque.
* **Unverified in real Word:** everything under "To check in real Word (tables, consolidated)"; the PRIORITY list in
  `tb-README.txt` is the order to take them in.

### Known items from C1

* **Literal tab in a word count (pre-existing, not changed).** A literal tab inside one `w:t` (`tab\there`, not
  `<w:tab/>`) is read as a raw level-`r` inline; `WordCount.para` counts it as nothing, so `tab` + `here` is one word
  and the tab is not a character, while the XML walk of an Opaque block counts a tab. The fix is one line (walk raw
  level-`r` inlines with `xml()`) but changes top-level counts; left for the owner to decide.
* The guide's numbering was changed in C2.6 (R19): part 10 Tables, parts 10..18 became 11..19, and again in Batch D
  P5.3 (R4): parts 11..13 new, 11..19 became 14..22 (see "Final guide parts").

## Batch D in brief: what to read first

Batch D (one batch: pages, headers and footers, fields, columns, line numbers, floating pictures and tables with text
wrap, Web layout and Outline) is described rule by rule in "Pages (Batch D)", "Fields (Batch D)", the data model's
`stories` and "Typed section fields", and the module table (every Batch D module row says its task, `Batch D Pn.k`,
and the decision it builds, `Dn`). This section is the map.

* **The decisions D1..D37** (the spec, `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-11-word-batch-d-design.md`, local): D1 galley
  then pages (`Paginate`, `PageGalley`); D2 the `Pages`/`Page`/`Frame` shapes; D3 section geometry in the galley
  (`SectGeom`, `SectWidth`); D4 one placement for screen geometry (`Place`, `PlaceDraft`, `PlacePrint`); D5 filling
  (`PageFill`, `PageCursor`); D6 keep rules (`PageKeep`); D7 incremental and lazy (`PageReuse`, `PageRecord`,
  2 ms slices, frames on demand); D8 tables across pages (`PageRows`, `PageCells`, `TblPieces`); D9 stories
  (`StoryRead`, `doc.stories`); D10 writing (`StoryWrite`: an untouched story byte for byte); D11 ids and scanners
  over stories; D12 ops with `story`, `setStory` (`OpsStory`, `OpsPath`); D13 which header on which page (`HdrPick`,
  `PageHF`); D14 editing them (`StoryFacade`, `HdrCmd`, `HdrMode`, `HdrStep`); D15 `FieldScan`; D16 `FieldParse`;
  D17 `Fields.REGISTRY`; D18 the computed display, codes and shading (`FieldShow`, `FieldPass`, `FieldView`); D19
  Update and Insert (`FieldCmd`, `FieldUpdate`, `FieldBox`); D20 typed section fields (`ReadSect`, `WriteSect`);
  D21 Page setup and Layout boxes (`PageBox`, `LayoutBox`, `SectSetup`, `SectLayout`); D22 even/odd page breaks;
  D23 columns (`PageCols`, `ColPass`, `PageBands`, `SectCols`, `ColumnsBox`); D24 line numbers (`LineNumbers`,
  `LineNumBox`); D25 anchors read (`AnchorRead`, `AnchorParts`); D26 placed (`AnchorPlace`); D27 wrap (`LineShape`,
  `WrapPass`, `AnchorMove`); D28 Wrap text (`WrapCmd`, `WrapXml`, `WrapMenu`); D29 the View menu (`ViewMenu`,
  `ViewMode`); D30 Print layout (`PageSheet`, `PagePaint`); D31 Web layout (`WebLayout`, `WebView`); D32 Outline
  (`OutlineLayout`, `OutlineFold`, `OutlineCmd`, `OutlineEdit`, `OutlineMenu`); D33 positions `{id, off}` in stories
  (`StoryPos`, `SelPage`); D34 scrolling and the extent; D35 line heights from the fonts (`FontMetrics`); D36 the
  hooks for later batches (D36's `G.reserve` for footnotes was removed in Batch E2: see "Footnotes and endnotes (Batch E2)"); D37 the performance budgets (below).
* **The plan's rulings R1..R12 as built:** R1 one batch, task ids `Pn.k`; R2 F9 stays Redo (as !Edit), Shift+F9 is
  View > Field codes, Edit > Update field and Update all fields have no key, Ctrl+Shift+Enter is a column break
  outside a table (Split table inside one); R3 hand-off ids PG / HF / CL (spec ids printed beside them, "HF3 (spec
  PG15)"); R4 the guide renumbered once (parts 11 pages, 12 headers, footers and fields, 13 columns, line numbers and
  text wrap; old 11..19 now 14..22); R5 floating tables placed in Print layout with text wrapped round them, every
  Table command inside; their edges drag (owner ruling at review P12b: all borders, never the position, `tblpPr`
  untouched); R6 `Page.top`, `w`, `h` in px; R7 `SettingsRead` (`onOffOf`, `viewOf`); R8 story addressing
  (`OpsUtil.locate(doc, pos, end, story)`); R9 `assets/disc` committed in the docs tasks only; R10 the page-start
  pin `pageStarts` asserted equal; R11 the hand-off XSD filter `/^(tb|pg|hf|cl)-.*\.docx$/`; R12 every galley root
  item carries `s`.
* **Data model additions:** `doc.stories` (a `Map` part -> `Story {blocks, rels, relsPart, root, prolog, orig,
  bytes}`) and `meta.storyParts`; typed section fields in `props` (`pgSz`, `pgMar`, `cols`, `lnNumType`,
  `pgNumType`, `titlePg`, `vAlign`, `type`, with `units` for Strict lengths; raw `extra` kept); ops carry an optional
  `story` (a part name; absent = the body) and `setStory {part, story, at?}` adds, replaces or removes a whole story;
  header and footer references stay raw in `props.extra`, read and written only through `SectRefs`.
* **The hand-off index** (PG, HF, CL, with their files and what !Letters does now) is "To check in real Word (Batch
  D)" below; the files come from `node tests/moreapps/handoff-pages.mjs` (local).
* **Performance (D37), the final figures:** the 50,000-paragraph Draft relayout +1.4 to +2.2 ms against main (P14.1,
  budget +5); Print layout open 53.6-57.9 ms over Draft's (ceiling 150), a convergent keystroke +3.2-4.2 ms (paired,
  ceiling 5), a line added at the top 0.11-0.15 ms for the first pages and 52.9-59.5 ms for all (ceiling 300); 100
  pages with a float on each, a keystroke beside a float 2.82 ms and in a floating table's cell 2.74 ms (ceiling 30);
  line numbers on page ~800 at most +1 ms; unequal columns over 50,000 paragraphs settle in the background over
  20-30 s of slices (the caret's page within 40 ms). Details: "The 50,000-paragraph document" and each section's
  Cost line.
* **User guide:** `$.Docs.Letters` parts 2 (the four views, Outline's keys and menu), 11, 12 and 13, and 20 (what is
  coming: tracked changes, printing; footnotes and endnotes came in Batch E2, part 24, and tables of contents, captions and cross-references in Batch E3, part 25).

## Pages (Batch D): the rules

Pagination is a second pass over the galley (D1): `Paginate.nextPage` cuts the root column into pages as CURSORS
(`PageCursor`: `{k, line, dy?, cuts?}`, root item k, its line (a table's row), px of a cut line or block already
shown, the cuts of a split table row), never re-breaking a
line or moving an item; `Pages` keeps the pages and works them out as they are asked for. P2.1 is the cursor pass,
P2.2 the keep rules, P2.3 reuse and 2 ms slices, P2.4 frames and fragments on demand, `ofPos`, `atScreen` and the
oracle pin; the Print layout view (P3) comes later. The galley a real document gives is `PageGalley.galleyOf(L)`.

The shapes (D2 + R6): `Pages {count, done, at(i), ensure(i), step(ms), num(i), finish(), kept, version, ofPos(pos,
aff), atScreen(x, y), fragsBuilt}`; `Page {i, s, num, fmt, parity: 'odd'|'even', first, blank, size {w, h} twips, mar {top, right, bottom,
left, header, footer, gutter} twips, start, end: Cursor, top, w, h (px), bodyTop, frameH, y0, vShift, why}` and `frames`
(P2.4, below; `header`, `footer`, `floats`, `numbers` in later tasks). `top` is the page's top edge on the Print layout sheet: the
sum of the earlier SHOWN pages' `h` + `PAGE_GAP` (16 px) each.

* **The frame** is the page height less the body top and bottom: body top = `max(mar.top, mar.header + header
  height)`, bottom likewise with the footer (an exact, negative, top or bottom margin: `mar.top`/`mar.bottom` only);
  at least `Paginate.MIN_FRAME`, 48 px (720 twips, half an inch: two body lines of 12 pt text), and `MIN_FRAME` when
  the sum is not a finite number (P2 fix wave, review I3). Our choice, not Word's (Page Setup in Word refuses
  margins that leave no text area; what it does with such a file is not known: hand-off question PGX1): margins at or over the page height
  (`pgMar` top and bottom 16000 on A4, or -16000) used to give a 1 px frame, so every 19 px line was cut over 19
  pages (50,000 paragraphs: 950,000 pages, 1.3 GB). With the floor every frame holds an ordinary line whole, so a
  page always takes at least one line and the count stays at most one a paragraph (50,000 paragraphs: 25,000 pages
  in about 110 ms). The frame is then taller than the page's room for it: it is drawn past the page bottom. The header and footer heights come from `G.hdrH(s, type)` / `G.ftrH(s, type)`, `type`
  `Paginate.typeAt`'s (P7.2, the galley of `PageHF.printGalley`: `HdrPick.typeOf`, `first` with titlePg on the
  section's first page, `even` with evenAndOddHeaders on an even NUMBER, else `default`; a fake galley without
  `typeOf`: `first` on a section's first page, `even` on an even number); the height is that of the story the page
  shows (`HdrPick.refOf`), laid out at the section's text width (`StoryLayout`), from its first item's space before
  to its last item's space after; 0 for no header, an empty one, or a part kept as bytes. `Paginate.frameOf` is the
  one rule; pages kept from an older pagination are checked against it (`PageRecord.hfAlike`, review focus 3: a
  header edited changes no body item).
* **Filling:** from the start cursor, an item whose `y + h` is within the frame goes whole (its gaps included);
  only the item crossing the bottom is looked at line by line (`PageCursor.lastFit`, a binary search over line
  bottoms). The space after a page's last paragraph may hang below the frame (it is not carried over). Galley gaps
  are placed as they are, except the band of a CONTINUOUS section break (`facts.band`, the `SectDeco` band in the
  item before's `gapBelow`): the frame reaches that much further. Other break gaps (`SectDeco` bands of page-starting
  sections, `FlowDeco`'s 12 px) always fall between pages, above the first item's `y`, so they are never placed.
* **Forced breaks:** a line ending in a page or column break (`facts.brPage`; a column break, `facts.brCol`, ends
  only its column on a page with columns, P10.1, below; in a section without columns it acts as a page break, as
  Word's does) ends the page after it; page break before (`facts.breakBefore`) starts a
  new page unless the paragraph is already first on its page (no empty page); a section starting with any type but
  `continuous` (nextPage, an absent or unknown one, evenPage, oddPage; nextColumn unless a column of the page is
  left, P10.1) starts a new page;
  a continuous section with another page size (w or h) does too (PG4). `Paginate` reads section starts from `it.s`
  (R12) and the type from `G.sect(s).type`.
* **Blank pages (PG3):** an evenPage / oddPage section whose first page's NUMBER would have the wrong parity gets
  ONE blank page before it (`blank: true`, `start` = `end`, the previous section's `s`, size and number + 1). Its
  number is used up (the next page's is one more: an odd page section after page 1 starts on page 3) and it is not
  shown: `top` does not move past it. Never two blanks in a row; with a restart that keeps the parity wrong the
  blank is still added once (no loop).
* **Page numbers:** one more than the page before; on a section's first page the section's `pgNumType` `start` when
  given. `first` (`Paginate.firstAt`, the one rule; `PageReuse` uses it for the pages it takes): the document's first
  page, or a page that starts at its section's first item (P7 fix I2). A continuous section that starts part way down
  a page has no first page: that page is the section before's (its header, footer and number), the next page starts
  inside the section and is not first, so it shows no first-page header (titlePg) and no number restart is made
  there; what Word does is hand-off question HFX1 (no spec id). Shown (`num(i)`) in the section's `fmt` when it is
  decimal, upperRoman, lowerRoman, upperLetter or lowerLetter, else decimal (thaiNumbers and every other format,
  `none` and `bullet` too: PG16), through `NumFormat.formatNumber`. `parity` follows the number.
* **Space before at the top of a page** is dropped after a natural break (`y0` is the galley y of the first line's
  top, so the next items move up; the galley is not changed) and kept after a page break, page break before, a
  section start, a blank page and on the first page (Word 2013+; PG5). When the space before kept at the top
  leaves the first line no room (the space alone, or the space and the line, taller than the frame) it is dropped
  all the same (`y0` moves to the line's top) and the item is fitted again: a line no taller than the frame is
  never cut (P2 fix wave, review I1).
* **Cuts:** an item (a picture, a box; a table is broken by rows instead, below) or a line taller than the frame is cut at the frame bottom
  when it is first on its page: the next page starts at the same item and line with `dy` px more shown. A frame
  always takes something (a line, an item, a cut), so every page moves on (`paginate.test.mjs` checks 200 random
  galleys). Zero-height items always fit. A value that is not a finite number never stops a page moving on (one
  rule, `PageFill`'s `px`): a cut ends once its `dy` reaches the `px` height of the block or line (0 when not
  finite), so a block or line whose height or galley y is NaN or infinite ends at once or after its height, and
  `used` is `px` (so `vShift` stays finite); the frame height is `MIN_FRAME` when not finite (above). `pages-cover.test.mjs` checks 3,000 random galleys (space before taller
  than the frame, tall lines and blocks, keep flags, breaks, sections): every line no taller than its frame is in
  the frags of exactly one page and whole inside its frame; the pieces of a taller one cover it.
* **Vertical alignment (PG6):** a page that ends its section (`why` `'section'`) or the document (`'end'`) and whose
  section has `vAlign` center or bottom gets `vShift` = half or all of the frame left over (`frameH - used`; `used`
  leaves out the bands not placed); 0 on every other page. `both` (spread between paragraphs) is not done yet: 0.
  `Paginate.shiftOf` is the one rule. A known limitation, taken literally from D5: Word is believed to align EVERY
  page of a vAlign section, a cover page ended by a plain page break included, where we shift only its last page;
  that variant is hand-off question PG6a (P2 review M1).
* **Keep rules (D6, `PageKeep`), at the item crossing the bottom only:**
  * *Widow and orphan control* (`widowControl`, on unless a layer turns it off): a paragraph is never split to
    leave its first line alone at the bottom or its last line alone at the top. A 2-line or 3-line paragraph moves
    whole; when one line would go over, one more goes with it (5 lines with room for 4: 3 and 2). Lines of exact
    height count the same. With it off the split is where the frame ends (4 and 1).
  * *Keep lines together* (`keepLines`): the paragraph moves whole unless its rest is taller than a frame; then
    it splits as if the flag were off (widow control still applies).
  * *Keep with next* (`keepNext`): when the crossing item moves whole to the next page (no line of it is left
    here, or a block that does not fit), the chain of keepNext items just before it goes with it: a heading moves
    with its body's first line, three headings in a row together. The chain is followed back over at most one frame
    of height (`chainStart`: one frame of items + 1 looked at); a chain taller than a frame, or one that reaches
    back to the page's first item, is ignored and the page breaks at the frame bottom (Word ignores the rule then),
    so 200 keepNext paragraphs give full pages and no loop. A table whose every row's paragraphs keep with next
    (`keepTable`) keeps with next the same way (PG7). A split paragraph needs nothing: its last lines are on the
    next page with the next block.
  * The rules never empty a page: on the page's first item the lines that fit are placed all the same (a 1-line
    frame takes one line a page). A page break inside a paragraph counts as its end for widow control.
  * Real documents resolve the flags through styles as page break before does (`FlowDeco.flagOf`: the last of the
    document defaults, the style chain and the paragraph's own that says); the fakes (`page-fixtures`) carry
    `keepNext`, `keepLines`, `widow` on their items. Cost: one more binary search in the crossing item (the lines
    a whole frame holds) and the bounded chain scan. The keep rules added 5 pages over the corpus (2,051 without
    them at P2.2, 2,056 with them; 2,058 since the empty page after a final page break, P2.4: see Cost).
  * PG1 (widows, headings), PG1a (widow control when nothing sets it), PG1b (3 lines, room for 2) and PG7 (keepNext
    tables) ask real Word.
* **The footnote hook (D36) is gone (Batch E2):** Batch D left `G.reserve(frame, refs)`, called per item, returning 0.
  Footnotes are placed by a page-level settle around `fillPage` (`NotePlace.settle`: an initial placement of the
  carried-in notes, a reserve per try, at most `MAX_TRIES` = 5 fills a page, the last fitting solution kept, the rest
  of a cut note carried over a parity blank page, the reuse record of every note looked at, and an empty foot of
  height 0 for a page that looked at notes and shows none); see "Footnotes and endnotes (Batch E2): what changed in
  existing modules".
* **Cost:** per page a walk over its items (O(1) each: facts memoised per item object, page break lines per lines
  array) and two binary searches in the crossing item: O(items on the page) a page, not D7's O(log n + k) (a binary
  search for the crossing item), so O(n) for the whole pass, which is inside the budget (P2 review M5). 10,000 page
  breaks in one paragraph give 10,000 pages in well under 200 ms; the whole corpus (719 files read, 2,058 pages
  with the fake measurer, the count `pages-corpus.test.mjs` prints) paginates in about 10 ms (median of 9 passes
  after layout, P2 fix wave), the slowest file 3.5 ms; the 50,000-paragraph document (1,667 pages) in about 45 ms.
* **Reuse (D7, P2.3, `PageReuse`; P2 fix wave):** a new `Pages(G, prev)` for a layout made from `prev`'s keeps, by
  identity, every page of `prev` whose breaks looked only at items before `L.dirtyFrom` (`seen < dirtyFrom`: a page
  that ends at a section start, a page break before or a keep chain looked at the item after its end, so it is
  worked out again when that item changed), and resumes after them. Each page it then works out is compared with
  `prev`'s at the same place (item k, `prev`'s item k - delta, delta the change in item count; the same line and
  cut): when k is at or past `L.cleanFrom` (the galley from there is `prev`'s moved by a constant) and the page is
  alike (every field but `i`, `num`, `top` and `y0`: blank, first, parity, section, `fmt`, `size`, `mar`, page and
  frame, body top, `why`, its end moved by delta; and its `y0` moved exactly as its item did), pagination has
  CONVERGED. The page just worked out is the new Pages' (`prev`'s own object when every field is the same), and
  `prev`'s pages after it are taken: as they are when nothing moved (no item count change, the same i, number, top
  and y0, `fmt`, `size` and `mar` what G gives now: `PageRecord.sectAlike`), else as new frozen pages
  (`PageRecord.pageOf`) with cursors moved by delta and `i`, `num`, `parity`, `first`, `top`, `y0` worked out again
  by `Paginate`'s own rules (`numberOf`, `topOf`, `startY`) and `fmt`, `size`, `mar` from G. A blank page is always
  worked out again (`nextPage`, which decides it before any fill): it carries the section BEFORE its start, which
  may have changed (review I2 a). Never by adding a difference: the result deep-equals a fresh pagination's, with no
  tolerance (`pages-reuse-prop.test.mjs`). Three kinds of page are not taken, because a field of theirs comes out of
  their own fill: a page whose `y0` `startY` did not give (the space before dropped at the top, I1; review I2 b), a
  page with a `vShift` (`Paginate.shiftOf`: the last page of a vAlign section, its shift from the px it used, whose
  floating-point value a fresh pass could give a hair differently; I2 c) and one whose `first` changed. Pagination
  works such a page out and converges again on it at once, so the pages after it are still taken. A cut's `dy` is the
  dy it started with plus the frame's room (`PageFill`), never a difference of galley y's, so it is the same
  wherever the galley puts the item and a page taken with it is exact. `prev` may be unfinished: its pages are taken
  as far as it got and the rest worked out. Nothing of `prev` is changed; the new Pages lets go of it once it is used
  up or the new Pages is done. Typing in a paragraph of a 100-page document: pages before it kept, the page after
  converges (`kept` 99); a paragraph inserted on page 40: the later pages kept with their cursors one item on
  (`pages-incr.test.mjs`). Cost of a convergent keystroke in the 50,000-paragraph document (1,667 pages, every page
  taken): 1.9 ms median, 0.35 ms more than before the fix wave (the `fmt`/`size`/`mar` check per page).
* **Slices (D7):** `ensure(i)` works out through page i at once (the visible pages); `step(ms = 2)` works out pages
  for at most `ms` (at least one) and returns `done`, for the window to call once a frame until done (P3/P5). A line
  added at the top of the 50,000-paragraph document (1,667 pages, no convergence: every page moves by one
  paragraph): `ensure(2)` 0.1 ms, all of it in 2 ms slices 46-50 ms (21-24 slices) on an idle machine, equal to a
  fresh pagination (the P2 review measured a fresh cursor pass at about 96 ms on a loaded machine: the D37 budget
  of +150 ms for the pass holds either way, with less room than the idle figure suggests).
* **Frames and fragments (D2, D7, P2.4, `PageFrames`):** `pg.frames` is not one of the Page's own fields but a
  getter: the first time it is asked for, the `Pages` holding the page (the newest one that took it) builds the
  page's frames and caches them for that page (so per `Pages.version`: a new layout's Pages builds new ones, even
  for a page it kept by identity); `Pages.fragsBuilt` counts the pages it built them for (the cursor pass of 1,500
  pages builds none). A blank page has none; every other page one frame `{x, y, w, h, start, end,
  frags}`: x and w the section's first column, y `bodyTop`, h `frameH`, start and end the page's; a page with
  columns (P10.1) one per column filled, x, w, start and end the column's. A `Frag {id, l0, l1,
  x, y}` is a root item's lines l0..l1-1 on the page (a block without lines: 0, 0; a table also `r0, r1, from?, cuts?,
  heads?`: P4.1, below) by item id, so a
  page kept from an older layout finds the new item through `L.byId`; `y` is where the item's galley top falls on
  the page (px from the page's top edge): `bodyTop + vShift + it.y - y0` (the page's y0, or its column's), less the bands of continuous
  section breaks between the page's first item and this one, plus `PageRows.adjOf` on a page that starts inside a
  table (P4.1); line j is at `y + lines[j].y`. A page that starts in
  an item has the item's top above the frame (the dropped space before, the lines on the page before); a cut line
  or block is in the frags of every page it shows on, every other line in exactly one.
* **Positions and points (P2.4, `PageFind`):** `ofPos(pos, aff = 'down') -> i` finds the root item holding the
  position (a cell's paragraph: its table, by flow index; P4.1: the row, cell and cell line, so a position in a
  split table is on the page of its row and cell line) and the line its caret is on (`PositionMap.lineOf`), then
  the last page starting at or before that place (binary search over the start cursors; a cut's later pages start
  after it; a blank page is never the answer), working out pages until one starts past it; -1 for an unknown id or
  bad input. `atScreen(x, y) -> {i, x, y} | null`: the page whose sheet rectangle (y from `top` to `top + h`, x from
  0, the page's left edge, to `w`) holds the point, and the point on the page; null in the 16 px gap, beside or
  past the pages or for a non-finite point; a blank page is never hit. Pages are worked out only as far as y.
* **A page break as the last thing (P2.4):** a page whose last line ends in a page (or column) break and which ends
  the galley has one more, EMPTY, page after it (`start` = `end` = the galley's end, `why` `'end'`, no frags):
  Word's, decided against the oracle (both corpus files ending in a page break, Word 2007 `style/2.docx` and
  `style3.docx`, have app.xml `Pages` 3 for 2 recorded content pages). This rests on two Word 2007 (compat 12) files
  whose app.xml `Pages` may be stale (SDK-made files often carry an old count), and Word 2013+ (compat 15) keeps the
  paragraph mark on the break's line and may not add the page: PG40 (hand-off question), "trailing page break",
  asks real Word, in compat 12 and 15, whether the empty page is shown; the rule may come to depend on the compat
  mode (P2 review M2). `Paginate.endsGalley(pg,
  n)` is the one rule for "no page after this one" (`Pages`, `PageReuse`). `ofPos` of the paragraph's end gives the
  page of the break's line.
* **Placement (P3.1, D4, `Place`, `PlaceDraft`):** a screen position is asked of the layout's `L.place`, never
  worked out from `it.y` / `ln.y` in a consumer. `DocHit.caretRect` puts the caret at `lineAt(it, line).x + its x in
  the line` and `lineAt(...).y` (a table's rows moved by `shiftOf`), `boxRect` at `lineAt(it, 0)`; `hitTest` maps
  the point to the galley first (`hit(x, y)`, then less `shiftOf`) and runs the galley rules on it;
  `selectionRects` puts each lit line where `rects(it, k, k + 1)` puts it (`PositionMap.selectionRects` now gives
  each rectangle's `line`), table boxes moved by `shiftOf` (P3.5: the screen band y0..y1 is made the galley span it
  shows by `L.place.band` first); Up and Down take the goal x from the line's `lineAt` (`SelVert.enter`, `SelTable.vertical`);
  the ruler's column x is the caret line's `lineAt` x; the work area's extent is `L.place.extent()`. In Draft
  every answer is exactly today's (the draft-layout and notable-layout snapshots, layout-prop). The gate
  `place-gate.test.mjs` counts `it.y`, `ln.y` and `.y +` per module against an allow-list (galley modules for
  good; painting and dragging until P3.2; the selection band until P3.5, for good since).
* **Painting and the pointer through Place (P3.2, D4):** `DocPaint.paint` asks `L.place.visible(y0, y1)` for the
  fragments a band shows and paints each in its GALLEY coordinates (`ItemPaint.paintPara(L, g, it, rect, l0, l1)`:
  only the fragment's lines, each at `PlaceDraft.lineTop`; `TablePaint`, `TblCellPaint`, `MarkPaint`, `BorderPaint`,
  `PicPaint` unchanged in what they draw) with the context translated by the fragment's dx, dy and rect moved back by
  them; a fragment not moved (every one in Draft) is painted with no `save`/`translate`/`restore` at all, so Draft
  makes exactly the calls it made (`itempaint.test.mjs`; the six browser suites the same counts and lines). The kept
  block's grey box is `DocHit.boxAt(it, x, y)` at its galley place (`boxRect` is the same rule at `lineAt`). The
  pointer: `PicFind.picAt`, `LinkFind.linkUnder`, `SelTable.zoneAt` and `TblEdge.edgeAt` take the work-area point and
  map it with `Place.toGalley` on the way in (as `DocHit.hitTest` does), then their galley rules; a picture's box
  (`picAt`, `selectedPic`, so the handles and `PicDrag`'s ghost) is at `L.place.lineAt` of its line; `TblDrag`'s ghost
  line at the table's `lineAt` (a row's bottom moved by `shiftOf`); `EditView.hitAt` is `L.hitTest`; `EditPaint`'s
  `pageRect` stays window geometry (Draft's one tall page; Print layout's pages are P3.3's `PagePaint`). The gate's
  allow-list now holds only `until '-'` entries (galley modules, answered rectangles, fragment painters, finders at a
  galley point; `place-gate.test.mjs` also checks the finders call `toGalley` and `DocPaint` `visible`); P3.5 made
  DocRects' entry one of them (it culls the galley band `L.place.band` gives) and the gate takes no other kind. A Print fragment's dx, dy are whole pixels (P3.3: the painters round in galley coordinates, then
  the translation adds dx, dy); `g.translate` joins D36's 2D subset (see the next point).
* **Print layout placed and painted (P3.3, D4, D30, D36; `PlacePrint`, `PageSheet`, `PagePaint`):**
  `Place.placeOf('print', L, P)` gives `PlacePrint`. A line's place is its fragment's on its page: the page holding
  it (a binary search over the page cursors), x = `it.x + dx`, y = its galley top + dy, where dx, dy = the page's
  place on the sheet + `round(frag.x - item x)`, `round(frag.y - item y)` (whole pixels, so a line is within half a
  pixel of `page.top + frame.y + vShift + (its galley top - page.y0)` below `L.top + PAGE_TOP`). An item in a cell
  moves with its table. Pages lie down the sheet from `L.top + PAGE_TOP`, `PAGE_GAP` (16) between them, each centred
  in the view (`MARGIN` at least from its left; P2.4's `atScreen` x runs from the page's left, so callers subtract
  it), edges on whole pixels; a blank page is not shown. `hit` takes the page at y, in the desk between pages the
  nearer one (the upper on a tie), above the first page its first line, below the last its last; on the page, the
  first line whose bottom is below y (a page with nothing on it, after a final page break: the last line before
  it). `rects` gives one box per page a range of lines is on, never one over the gap. The extent is as far as the
  pages worked out so far (lazy, D34) and `PAGE_TOP` more, as wide as the view or the widest section's page centred.
  A cut line or block (taller than the room) is drawn in both pages' fragments, each clipped to its frame
  (`clip`). `EditPaint.paintView` in Print layout (L.place has `pages`): the desk, then `PagePaint.paintPages` (each
  page in rect: sheet, corner marks, then `paintPage` with the context at the page's origin, cut to the page's
  height) instead of the one tall page, and the selection culled to `L.place.band` (the galley span of the lines
  shown; since P3.5 `DocRects` asks it itself). Breaks in Print layout draw no rule unless `opts.marks`
  (View > Formatting marks, P3.4): `DocPaint.paintFrags(..., {marks})` passes `rules` to `ItemPaint.paintPara` (a
  page or column break's rule) and draws a section break band only with the fragment holding its item's end
  (`tail`) and a "Page break before" rule only with the one holding its top (`head`): once each. Draft's calls are
  unchanged (marks default on, no `head`/`tail`/`clip`). Painting a band builds frames for the pages it shows only
  (`pagepaint.test.mjs`: a 1,500-page document, a 600 px band, `fragsBuilt` <= 2). `DocPaint` translates moved
  fragments (`g.translate`) and clips cut ones (`rect`, `clip`), and `PagePaint` clips and translates to the page:
  Batch G's 2D subset (D36) needs `translate`, `beginPath`, `rect` and `clip` besides the calls D36 lists, or an
  adapter that offsets. Not yet: a paragraph's border box and shading split across pages are drawn whole on each
  page (cut at the page's edge only; PG38's per-page boxes are later); a break rule inside a table cell is drawn
  regardless of the marks; with the marks on, a continuous section break's band may overlap the next line on the
  page (the band is not on the page, D5).
* **Views (P3.4, D29, D30, D34, OD2; `ViewMode`, `ViewMenu`, `PageInfo`):** the window menu has View after Insert:
  Print layout, Web layout (P13.1), Outline (P13.2), Draft, Formatting marks, Ruler (moved from Format). A
  window opens in its file's `w:view` (`print`; `normal` is Draft; `web` is Web layout (P13.1); `outline` and `masterPages` are Outline
  (P13.2)), else in the view chosen last in any window (`Choices:Letters` `view`), else in Print layout.
  The view is never written to the file: the bytes saved are the same in every view (`word-pages.mjs`). In Outline, Tab / Shift+Tab at a heading's start and Ctrl+Shift+Up / Down are the outline commands (P13.3, `OutlineCmd`). The caret never stays in hidden text (P13 fix I1): `EditView.placed` (after every layout) and `setSelection` apply `OutlineFold.shownSel`; `setSelection` (Find, Go to) and `FindSel.all` first call `view.reveal` (`OutlineView`), which opens the headings over the target; Enter at the end of a `+` heading and Backspace / Delete next to hidden text go to `OutlineEdit`. Switching
  keeps the selection and puts the caret's line at the same height in the window. Print layout's pages are worked
  out lazily: `fit` makes a `Pages` for each new layout from the last one's (D7) and a `PlacePrint` on it; painting
  and the caret work out the pages they need; the rest are worked out in 2 ms slices, one an animation frame, and
  each slice that adds pages sets the extent again (it grows; nothing above moves) and the info line; keys and edits
  go between slices (a slice after an edit lays the edit out first); closing the window stops them. The info line
  is a display field at the end of toolbar row 2
  (`pageInfo`, 216 px): `Page 3 of 12`, `Page 3 of 12...` while pages are still being worked out, and ` (Section
  2)` with several sections; in Draft only `Section 2` (several sections) or nothing (Draft does no pagination,
  D37). Formatting marks is per window and off at first: in Print layout the breaks are drawn as labelled rules
  only with it on; Draft draws them always, as before. Test hooks: `task.word.docs[i]` `viewName`, `setView(v)`,
  `marks`, `setMarks(on)`, `pageInfo` (the field's text) and `view.pages()` -> `{count, done, caretPage}` (null
  in Draft). A caret moved past the extent's end (Ctrl-End before the slices have reached it: its caret rectangle
  works its pages out) sets the extent again before it is scrolled to (`EditScroll.scrollToCaret` calls
  `view.refit`, `ViewMode`'s `dw.fitExtent`). `!RunImage` waits for the choices as well as the fonts (at most
  2.5 s) before it makes a window, so the first document opened by a double-click gets the remembered view. In
  Print layout Ctrl-End shows the caret's line, not the bottom edge of a last page taller than the window. The
  browser suites written for Draft's geometry (their clicks and pixels worked out from the galley: 24 of them,
  from `word.mjs` to `word-tables-hostile.mjs`) start !Letters with Draft as the remembered view
  (`tests/moreapps/word-draft.mjs` `asDraft(page)`, writing `Choices:Letters` `{view: 'draft'}`); Print layout's
  own interaction is `word-pages.mjs`; P3.5 adds `WORD_VIEW=print` (below).
* **Caret, clicks and selections across pages (P3.5, D33, D34; `SelPage`, `PlacePrint` `area` and `edge`):**
  Up and Down go in flow order from a frame's last line to the next frame's first line (the next page's), the goal
  x taken relative to where `L.place` puts the line they land on (`SelTable.vertical` asks `lineAt` of the target
  line, not the current one; across items `SelVert.enter` always did). Ctrl+Page Down and Ctrl+Page Up (`Keys`
  `nextPage`, `prevPage`; Shift extends) put the caret at the start of the next / previous page's first line
  (`SelPage.toPage`: the first fragment of that page, a paragraph cut from the page before at the line the page
  starts with, a table entered at its first cell; blank pages passed; before the first page its first line; past
  the last page nothing moves); where there are no pages (Draft) they are Page Down and Page Up exactly as before
  (one rule: `SelMove.pageCmd(L, cmd)`, which `EditKeys` asks too; P3 fix wave M4). P3 fix wave (I2): Chrome and
  Firefox reserve Ctrl+PgDn / Ctrl+PgUp (their next / previous tab, like Ctrl-Tab), so the keys never reach the page
  in a normal tab (hand-off question PGX5); Edit > Next page and Previous page (after Replace..., keys shown `Ctrl+PgDn` / `Ctrl+PgUp`, never
  shaded; Word keeps browse-by-page under Go To in its Edit menu) run `EditKeys.pageMove(view, cmd)`, the keys' own
  path (in Draft a window down / up); the guide, `!Help` and README say a browser may keep the keys. No core change
  can help (the browser never sends them). `SelPage.firstOn` passes the rest of a table or kept block started on a
  page before (a fragment with `head` false has no caret place there: `SelTable.enter` would go back to the table's
  first cell on its first page, and the next press came back to the same page): the fragment after it is taken, a
  page with nothing else is passed like a blank one, so every press moves on (`selvert.test.mjs`, a 150-row table
  over page tops; `word-pages-edit.mjs` the same in the desktop). P4.2: a fragment holding the rest of a table
  (`head` false, also a page starting in row 0 cut, `{line: 0, cuts}`) is entered at row r0's first cell with a
  line on that page (after `from`), so every page is reached (`selvert.test.mjs`, a row cut over many pages). Clicks: on a page, its nearest line; above the page's first line (its top margin) or
  below its last (its bottom margin), that edge line at the x clicked; in the desk between pages, the nearer page's
  edge line (`PlacePrint.hit` marks such a hit `edge`, and `Place.toGalley` keeps the galley point inside that
  line, so it never falls on a line of the next or previous page); above the document's first line or below its
  last (page 1's top margin, the last page's bottom margin and the desk past them) the document's start or end, as
  in Draft (a click under the text is its end); left or right of the text, the line's start or end. In a page's header area (from the header distance `mar.header` down to the body's top) or footer area (from
  the frame's bottom down to the footer distance) a click and a drag do nothing and a double-click enters the header and footer mode (`EditMouse` asks
  `hdrClick` first, `HdrMode`: P7.3, D14); the strips nearer the page's edges than the
  header and footer distances are margin and hit the edge line. A drag across pages auto-scrolls as before and the
  selection is lit per line on each page (`DocRects` culls the galley span `L.place.band` gives for the screen
  band, then `L.place.rects` boxes each line: never in the desk). The ruler's page is the caret's page in Print
  layout (`RulerInd.scaleOf`: its rectangle on the sheet, so a landscape section's page shows 11 in with 9 in of
  text); Draft keeps `L.pageLeft`, `L.pageW`. Scrolling (D34): the caret is kept on the screen as pages are worked
  out again after an edit far down a long document and after Ctrl-End (held by `word-pages-edit.mjs`; no change
  was needed in `EditScroll`). Zoom: the same clicks land on the same places at 50% and 200%. Known limit: a click
  4 px above a table that starts a page (its column zone, `SelTable.zoneAt`) is an edge hit, kept on the table's
  first row: it puts the caret in the cell instead of selecting the column.
* **Browser coverage of Print layout (P3.5):** `word-pages.mjs` (views), `word-pages-edit.mjs` (clicks, the desk, the

  still paginated. The filter is by path (`/corpus/handoff/`): never park a hand-off folder elsewhere under `corpus/`

  footers, `PageHF.printGalley`, as Print layout is: 206 without them; natural breaks 64 -> 67/514; 2,179 -> 2,212

* **Pages against hostile input (P5.1, `word-pages-hostile.mjs`):** every case opens in Print layout and is
  paginated to the end in well under a second (the 63-column table over 51 pages 0.65 s, 10,000 page breaks 0.35 s),
  with no error. What each gives: a page size of 0 is a real size, clamped for display (`SectGeom.pxOf`: the page
  MIN_PAGE_H 200 px high (hand-off question PGX2), so 1" margins leave a frame of `MIN_FRAME` 48 px: 80 paragraphs make 294 pages); -1 and
  "abc" are not values (`ReadSect`: an unsigned measure that is negative or not a number is kept raw, not read),
  so `SectGeom`'s default, A4 portrait, applies (2 pages); 1e9 is clamped to MAX_PAGE_H 20,000 px (one
  page); margins over the page give `MIN_FRAME` frames; a top margin of -31680 is exact (Word's) and its frame
  is clamped like any other (100 pages for 200 paragraphs); 10,000 page breaks give 10,001 pages (the empty page
  after a final break, P2.4); a 20,000 px picture (one line taller than any page) takes its page and the text goes on after
  it (4 pages for it and 40 paragraphs); a keepNext chain longer than a page breaks where the page is full; 500 sections of alternating sizes give
  500 pages; oddPage breaks back to back give a blank even page before each section (PG3). No product change was
  needed: the cases were held already by the P2 fix wave's guards (`MIN_FRAME`, the NaN guards) and `SectGeom`'s
  clamps. Saving never waits for pagination nor reads it (pagination never touches the model): Save and saveBytes
  begun while the slices run write the parts written once they are done.
* **Layout extras against hostile input (P14.1, `word-layout-hostile.mjs`):** every case opens in Print layout and
  its pages, column passes and wrap passes finish in well under a second, every page and float finite, typing at the
  end and undo exact: 45 columns with no spacing (each 0.14 in: laid out at `SectGeom.MIN_TEXT` 80 px and moved into
  the page, so they overlap, P10 fix M5), `w:num` 46 and 1e9 (kept raw, one column), unequal columns of 100 twips and
  1e9, 1,000 column breaks in two columns (501 pages), `lnNumType` countBy, start and distance 1e9 and start
  2147483647, 500 floating pictures on one page, wrap polygons of 4,096 points (`AnchorParts.MAX_POINTS`, used) and
  10,000 (not read: the picture stays in line, dashed), anchors with absurd offsets, unknown relativeFrom and align
  values and a 1,000,000 px picture, 200 floating tables on one page with `tblOverlap` never, floating tables at
  tblpX / tblpY 1e9 and -1e9, with no attributes and with bad values, a floating table nested in a floating table's
  cell, and 45 columns holding floats, floating tables, column breaks and line numbers together. Outline: 10,000
  paragraphs under nine levels of headings, every heading collapsed (only the 1,000 level 1 headings shown), expanded,
  Show level 1..9 and All, each step 15-85 ms. Web layout: 3,000 long paragraphs resized 100 times, the slices end with
  every line at the last width. 300 seeded random actions across the four views (typing, Enter, Delete, Backspace,
  column and page breaks, caret moves, Wrap text kinds, Outline promote / demote / move, collapse sets, zoom, window
  sizes, views, undo, redo, scrolling): the selection valid after each, nothing reported, undoing everything gives
  the opened model. The suite found no fault in the layout; writing the hand-off files found one in the Columns box
  (Left and Right refused on A4, fixed in `ColsVals`, above).
* **Tables across pages (D8, P4.1, `PageRows`):** row boundaries are break candidates. A table that fits goes whole
  (O(1)); for one crossing the bottom, a binary search over its rows finds the first row that does not fit, and only
  that row's cells are looked at. That row is:
  * *split* by default: each cell's column is cut at its own last line that fits (`cuts[c]` the first of its lines
    for the next frame, counted over the column's units: each line of a paragraph, each row of a nested table, one
    per other item; a nested table is kept whole on one side of the cut, PG11, unless it is taller than a frame:
    then it is cut between its rows where the cell reaches it (review P4 M2: before, the cell waited empty for a
    frame's top, where the nested table was shown clipped; `tblpage-nest.test.mjs`); a cell whose rest fits is not
    cut: its line count), measured as
    the part is drawn: a first part from the cell's column top (its first line's space before counted; review P4
    I2: it was measured from that line's top, so the cut lines and the cut edge's border ran past the frame), a rest
    from the line it starts with (`restH` the same: a cell with nothing shown before from its column top); a centre
    or bottom aligned cell is cut as if top-aligned (PG8); the top margin is repeated above the rest. The next page
    starts at `{k, line: r, cuts}`; the rest's height is the tallest remainder (`restH`), and the galley row height
    is not changed: the rows after it, and every item below on that page, move by `adjOf` (heads + rest - the row's
    height);
  * *moved whole* to the next page when it is `cantSplit` and no taller than a frame's room for a row (the frame less
    the repeated header rows), when it has an exact height (never split), or when no cell would show a line; the
    page then ends at the row (`{k, line: r}`), or before the table when it is row 0 (the keep chain is then asked,
    as for any item that moves whole);
  * *a box that does not fit (review P4 M1):* a cut part keeps the cell's bottom margin inside the frame (a line
    goes to the next frame when it and the margin do not fit). A row whose content fits but whose box does not (a
    trHeight atLeast taller than the room) moves whole to the next frame when it is not first in its frame and its
    box fits a frame; otherwise it ends the frame CUT TO ITS CONTENT (`cuts` every cell's line count): drawn to its
    content and bottom margin with its bottom border inside the frame, the rest of its height dropped; its rest on
    the next page is empty (not drawn; Ctrl+PageDown enters the next row). Before, such a row ended the page whole
    and its bottom and border were clipped. Word's own rule here is hand-off question PGX3. Test:
    `tblpage-box.test.mjs`;
  * *forced* at a frame's top (nothing can move it on): a cantSplit row taller than the room splits; an exact row is
    placed whole (taller than the frame: clipped, Word's way) and the next page starts at the next row; a cell line or
    nested table's row taller than the room is shown (clipped) and its cell moves on by it, so every page moves on.
  * *Header rows:* the leading `tblHeader` rows repeat at the top of every continuation frame (`heads`, frag field;
    a page starting at row r >= heads), unless they and the row after them do not fit the frame (`headsOf` 0; also
    none when every row is a header row). Repeated rows are drawn from the same row layout (P4.2) and take their
    height off the frame.
  * *keepNext tables (PG7):* a table whose rows all keep with next moves whole to the next page when it crosses the
    bottom (not split) unless it is taller than a frame, and is pulled to the next page with the next paragraph by the
    keep chain as before.
  * *Frags:* a table's frag adds `r0, r1` (rows r0..r1-1 on the page), `from` (the cuts row r0 continues after),
    `cuts` (the cuts row r1-1 is cut at), `heads` (the header rows repeated above r0), each only when there is one.
    Its `y` is where the table's galley top falls with the page's shift, so a row after the first is at `y + ry`.
    P4.2 draws and places them: see "Split rows painted and hit".
  * *Split rows painted and hit (P4.2, D8, D33; `TblPieces`, `TblPagePaint`, `PrintHit`, `PlacePrint`):* a page's
    table fragment is drawn piece by piece (`TblPieces.piecesOf`): the repeated header rows at the frame's top from
    the same row layout (no new item; not text of their own: a click there is the ORIGINAL header row's cell,
    PG10); whole rows as in Draft; a part of a cut row with its cells' shading and the row's borders on the part's
    box, the cut edge drawn as the row's bottom border on the first part and its top border on the next (PG9), and
    each cell's content moved to the part's top (top-aligned: a vAlign center / bottom cell too, PG8) and cut to
    the lines that part shows, so every line is drawn once. The caret, hits, selection rectangles and the info
    line's page use the same pieces: a cell's line is on the page of its row and cell line, a hit in a table
    fragment carries that piece's shift (`Place.toGalley`), a cell or row selection is one box per page part
    (`PlacePrint.rowParts`). Down from a cut cell's last line on a page goes to the same cell's continuation
    (PG35: galley order, placed on the next page). A vertically merged cell is drawn slice by slice (review P4
    I3): beside a run of whole rows its column is cut to the units of those rows (`PageCells.mergeCut`, through
    `TablePaint.paintRows`' `cut`), and a cut part of a row it spans shows that row's slice (a continue cell's part
    draws the merge's column, `TblPieces` cell `col`); a click there lands in the merged cell. Approximation: the
    table's outer box (cell spacing) is not closed at a page cut. Tests: `tblpagepaint.test.mjs`, `place.test.mjs` (tables across pages; the Consumer Confidence Report
    from the corpus when present), `selvert.test.mjs`, `word-pages.mjs` part 3.
  * *Border boxes cut by a page (PG38; `BorderGroups.closedMark`, `BorderPaint` l0..l1, `DocPaint`):* a bordered
    paragraph group (or one paragraph) split across pages is closed on each page part: the fragment first in its
    frame draws the box's top side (not `between`), the one last in its frame its bottom side, round the lines
    that fragment shows. The top edge of a continued part sits above its first line (no room is reserved for it).
    Draft is unchanged (its fragments carry no `first` / `last`). Test: `bordergroups.test.mjs`.
  * *Positions:* `Pages.ofPos` of a position in a cell is the page of its row and cell line (`PageCells.cellPlace`).
  * *Reuse:* a cursor's cuts are compared by value (`sameCursor`, `PageRecord.samePage`) and ordered by `cutOrder`;
    a table adopted from `prev` is the same block object laid out alike, so its cuts are too. `pages-reuse-prop`
    covers fake tables (splits, cantSplit, exact and header rows, nested blocks) and real ones edited in their cells.
  * *Not finite:* a unit's place or height that is not a finite number counts 0 (`px`), and `adjOf` is 0 unless
    finite; a table of NaN rows then moves on a line a page at worst, never stalls.
  * *Vertically merged cells (review P4 I3; `PageCells.unitsAt`, `needOf`):* a merged cell's units (its column's
    lines) belong to the rows of its span their TOPS lie in: the first row holds those above the second row's top,
    each continue cell the ones in its own row (the last row the rest). Each row then cuts its slice as any cell's
    lines, and a row whose slice runs past its box (a line whose top is in it) needs that much more (`needOf`: the
    row is cut, or the page ends before it, rather than clipping the line). Before, the whole merged cell was its
    first row's: the part of it beside rows on later pages was shown on no page. `PageCellAt.cellPlace` places a
    merged cell's line in its slice's row (the continue cell there), so the caret, Ctrl+PageDown (`SelPage`, by
    `PageCellAt.unitAt`) and `ofPos` agree with what is drawn (Word's way: hand-off question PGX4). Test: `tblpage-merge.test.mjs` (every line shown
    once, inside a frame, hit back: merges of 40 rows, a cut first row, random merges).
  * *Approximations:* a header row is split like any other row when the table starts low on a page. Cost: 63 columns x 500 rows (31,500 cells, some rows split) paginate with frames
    into 86 pages, 75 of them starting in a split row, in 3.8 ms median (fake galley, frame 930 px;
    `pagerows.test.mjs` asserts a median under 100 ms).
* **Page setup (P4.3, D21; `PageValues`, `SectSetup`, `PageBox`: the module row):** Format > Page setup... edits
  the paper size, orientation, margins and gutter of This section / This point forward / Whole document, and the
  document's gutter position, as one undo step. This point forward breaks at the caret as Insert > Section break >
  Next page does (so a caret inside a paragraph splits it; at the start of a non-empty paragraph an empty paragraph
  ends the section before), except at the very start of a section, where nothing is inserted. A raw `w:pgSz` or
  `w:pgMar` (one the reader did not understand) keeps every attribute when the box changes it: only the values
  changed are set in it, in twips (`PageValues.setPart`, the one rule of both boxes; review P4 M3: it was replaced
  by a typed one, losing the attributes not known). Its values are not read (the box shows the defaults for them). User guide: part 11, "Page setup" (P5.3).
* **Layout box and even/odd breaks (P4.4, D21, D22; `SectLayout`, `LayoutBox`: the module row):** Format > Layout...
  edits the CURRENT section's start (New page, Continuous, Even page, Odd page, New column), Different first page
  (`titlePg`), the header and footer distances from the page's edge and the vertical alignment, and the document's
  Different odd and even (`evenAndOddHeaders`), as one undo step. As in Page setup (`PageValues.setPart`), a raw
  `w:pgMar` keeps its unknown attributes: only the distance changed is rewritten in it. Insert > Section break > Even page / Odd page
  insert a break whose following section has `w:type` `evenPage` / `oddPage`; in Print layout the blank page a wrong
  parity needs is counted (the numbers skip it) but not shown (PG3). Different first page / odd and even change the
  headers and footers the pages show (P7.2; the Header menu sets them too, `HdrMenu`). User guide: part 11, "The
  Layout box" (P5.3; brought up to date in P9.4).
* **User guide (P5.3, R4):** part 11 of `$.Docs.Letters`, "Pages and page setup": Print layout and Draft (which view a
  window opens in, the info line, clicks and keys across pages, the browser caveat for Ctrl+Page Down / Up and the
  Edit menu route), where the pages break (forced breaks, the keep options, space before at a page top, even and odd
  breaks and the blank page counted but not drawn, page sizes per section, vertical alignment), tables across pages
  (split rows, cantSplit and exact rows, the atLeast rule, repeated header rows and the click that goes to the
  original row, merged cells flowing, nested tables, keepNext tables) and bordered groups closed per page, the Page
  setup box (Apply to, This point forward splitting the paragraph, the refusals) and the Layout box (Justified drawn
  as Top; P9.4: its header and footer settings now change the pages), and "How close to Word" (no exact equality
  promised; about three in ten (P5.3) of Word's recorded starts in the corpus matched within a line, nearly all forced
  ones, while about four in five natural ones are more than a line away; final fix B: a little over four in ten of the
  page and column starts, about seven in ten natural ones more than a line away, see "The oracle" (review P5 I2: never worded as small errors;
  part 22 and the README say the same); what is not on the pages yet and the approximations). Part 2 describes the View menu and the info line,
  part 3's key table the Ctrl+Page keys, part 8 the four section break kinds and the breaks in Print layout, part 6
  the flow options' effect, part 10 points at part 11, part 17 says the font metrics decide the page breaks, parts
  20 and 22 are brought up to date; part 13 holds one sentence until P14.2 (part 12 was written in P9.4, below). `!Help` has a Pages
  paragraph; the README a **Pages:** paragraph.
* **Newspaper columns (P10.1, D23; `PageCols`, `ColPass`):** a page of a section with two columns or more
  (`L.geom(s).cols`, `SectGeom`: `w:cols` `num` equal columns with `space` between, 720 twips when not given, or
  its typed `w:col` widths) fills its columns left to right, then the next page (`PageCols.fillCols`, from
  `nextPage`): each column is a frame of the page's own `bodyTop` and `frameH` (the header and footer are the
  page's), filled by `PageFill.fill` from where the column before ended, at its own galley y (`startY` with the
  column before as the page before: space before dropped after a natural break). A column goes on to the next
  when it was full (`why` `'full'` or `'cut'`: a cut item goes on down the columns), ended by a column break (a
  line in `facts.brCol`: `PageGalley` reads the break item's label, `BreakMarks.COLUMN_LABEL`), or before a
  section that starts `nextColumn` with the same page size; a page break, page break before, another section
