  start or the galley's end end the page, and so does anything in the last column (a column break there: the
  next page). The page carries `cols` (frozen `[{x, w, start, end, y0, used, why}]`, the columns filled; only on
  a page of a section with columns, so a one-column page's fields are as before); its `end`, `why` are the last
  column's, `used` the most any used, `seen` the furthest, `y0` the first's. Reuse: `PageReuse` compares the
  columns' cursors moved by delta (`colsAlike`) and moves them for a page it takes (`moveCols`, y0 worked out
  again; a column whose y0 came out of its fill is not taken), `samePage` compares them by value (`sameCols`).
  `Frames`: one per column (above). Placement (`PlacePrint`): a line is on the frag of the column whose start is
  the last at or before it (`PageFind.after`), `rects` and `rowParts` give a box per column, `PrintFrags` tags
  each frag with its frame's index `col`, and `PrintHit` hits in the column at x (its frame holds x, else the
  nearest one with something in it). The width (D23): the galley lays a section's paragraphs out at its first
  column's width (D3), so equal columns need nothing more; with unequal ones a paragraph that lands in a column
  of another width is laid out again at that width: `ColPass.colPass(L, P)` looks at the root paragraphs
  starting in each column of the pages worked out and gives the widths of one more layout (`L.colW`, `DocLayout`
  opts `colW`; `DocItems` gives such a paragraph `w` = `ColPass.widthOf`, and as `w` is in the reuse key only
  those paragraphs are broken again: keyed by width). **P10 fix I2: settled page by page.** Each width pass
  re-breaks paragraphs, which moves every later paragraph, so fixing all pages at once (P10.1, capped at 8 passes
  an edit) never settled past a few pages and gave history-dependent pages (15 pages after edits against 19 for
  the same document opened). Now `colPass(L, P, upTo)` works on the FIRST page not settled (pages before it stay
  as they are): (1) stale widths go back to the first column's width: a paragraph of the page or of the page after
  whose width was given neither by this page's settling nor (not as a guess) by the page before's (`colW.giver`:
  the serial of the settling that gave it); (2) on the page's first pass the widths are guessed ahead
  (`ColAhead.ahead`: the columns filled with each paragraph's text poured into lines of the column's width, up to
  the end of the page after it); (3) then each paragraph not at its column's width gets it, one going back to a
  width it had in this settling the narrower of the two, at most `MAX_TRIES` (4) widths a paragraph; a page not
  settled after `MAX_PAGE_PASSES` (6) passes in one `DocVersion`, or where nothing more can be tried, is left. A
  settled (or left) page is remembered (`colW.known`: its start, its columns' cursors and widths, the paragraphs
  it left), so an edit that moves no column break costs no pass; at most 2 x 6 passes a page worked out per
  version. `ViewMode` runs the passes due on the pages up to the caret's at once for at most `SYNC_MS` (40) ms
  after a new layout, and the rest in its slices for at most `TICK_MS` (8) ms a frame (`dw.colDue` keeps the
  slices going while passes are due after the pages are done); `dw.colW` is kept (`WinFit` passes it to every new
  layout). Measured (fake measurer, Node, `colpass-settle.test.mjs`; 3 unequal columns): a keystroke in Print
  layout (the layout, the caret's page, the passes up to it) 10,000 paragraphs settled, caret mid-document: 2.6 ms
  typing a character, 10-17 ms typing a line's worth each time (budget 40 ms); 50,000 paragraphs
  (`WORD_COLS_PERF=1`): 55-65 ms (budget 150 ms). Opening (passes in slices, CPU time): 10,000 paragraphs 340-470
  layouts for 223-236 pages, 1.5-2.5 s; 50,000 paragraphs about 1,230-1,770 layouts for 1,112-1,177 pages, 22-32 s
  (the slices run one or two passes a frame there; the pages near the caret first). Edited == fresh: a document
  edited (five edits that move lines) and the same document opened afresh give the same pages and widths (test,
  Left preset and 3 unequal columns); a random-edit fuzz of hostile documents (2 to 6 sections of 1 to 4 equal or
  unequal columns, 80 px columns, short pages) agrees in 35 of 40 seeds, and each of the 5 that differ holds a page
  left unsettled (a paragraph that fits a column only at another column's width after `MAX_TRIES` widths): its
  layout depends on the edit history (documented in the guide). Draft (and Web) show one column: `ViewMode` lays a layout with `colW` out again
  without it (`dw.colW` null). Format > Columns: P10.4 (`SectCols`, `ColumnsBox`). Insert > Column break: P10.3 (`InsertApply.columnBreak`, `EditKeys` routing Ctrl+Shift+Enter by the caret's place). Approximations: a paragraph that goes
  on from one column into another of another width keeps the lines of the column it starts in; only paragraphs
  are laid out again (a table keeps its section's first column's width); a column's frame is the page's.
  `w:equalWidth` absent: the `w:col` children are used when there are any (`SectGeom`; the schema gives no
  default, ECMA's text leaves it open; Word writes `equalWidth="0"` with `w:col` children and none for equal
  columns, 0 corpus files differ); Strict files' `w:cols w:space="36pt"` were raw until the P10 fix (I3: typed
  with their units now; every such corpus element is one column, so nothing is laid out differently). The oracle
  (`pagestarts.mjs ourStarts`) counts each column's start after the first, as Word records a
  `lastRenderedPageBreak` there too (`columns2.docx`: 51 in 18 pages of 3 columns); the pin was unchanged at P10.1
  (209, columns 9/203) only because of that counting: page starts alone scored 205 after P10 (P10 fix M2). Tests: `pagecols.test.mjs`, `viewmode-cols.test.mjs`, `colpass-settle.test.mjs`.
* **Balancing, continuous sections, lines between columns (P10.2, D23, PG25, PG26; `PageBands`, `PageCols.balance`):**
  a page is filled band by band (`PageBands.fillPage`, from `nextPage`): a band is the columns of one section
  (`colsAt`: one or more), filled by `fillCols` (`fill` for one column) with the room left on the page as its frame.
  `PageFill.fill` ends a frame before a continuous section (same page size) where the columns change: the section
  before it or it has two columns or more (`PageFill.contStart`, `why` `'cont'`; two one-column sections run on in
  one frame, as before). A band with two columns or more that ends so is balanced: `PageCols.balance(G, from,
  frames) -> frameH`, a binary search on the frame height between the content's height (the columns' `used`) /
  the section's column count and the room, at most `BALANCE_STEPS` (12) fills of the columns, each a cursor-only
  fill; the content fits when the fill ends at the same cursor, again before the continuous section, and no column
  ends `'cut'` unless the unbalanced fill had a cut too (P10 fix I1: a band holding less than a line a column, a
  heading, one paragraph, a tall picture or a table row, keeps the line whole in column 1, as Word does, instead of
  drawing its top in column 1 and its bottom in column 2); the band is
  then filled at the least height found (30 lines in 2 columns: 15 / 15; 31: 16 / 15). Only before a continuous
  break (PG26: not at the document's end, Word's rule; a section running over pages: its last page). The next
  band starts below the tallest column (`top` += the band's `used`) at `startY`'s galley y; a band after the first
  that takes nothing whole in its first column (no room for its first line: P10 fix I1 looks at the first column,
  as a cut going on down the columns drew one line in pieces across a band at the page's foot) is not placed, nor is one when no room is left: the page
  ends before it (`why` `'full'`) and the section starts the next page. Every column record now has `top` (px below
  `bodyTop`) and `h` (its band's frame: the room, or the balanced height); `sameCols` and `colsAlike` compare them;
  a page with two columns or more in any band has `cols` (every band's columns in order), one of one band of one
  column has none (fields as before); the page's `used` is the last band's top + used. `PageFrames`: a frame's y
  is `bodyTop + top`, h its `h`, and frags move by `top`; `PrintHit` picks the column whose frame holds the
  point, else the nearest by y, then x. The line between columns (PG25): `PagePaint.paintPage` draws, for each
  band (the columns sharing a `top`) whose section has `w:cols w:sep` on (`PageGalley` `sect(s).sep`), a 1 px
  (0.75 pt, `SEP_W`) black (`SEP_COLOUR`) line in the middle of the space between each two columns filled, from
  the band's top as long as its tallest column (the most `used`). The page-start pin moved from 209 to **323 of
  960** (columns 9 -> 85 of 203, natural 67 -> 105 of 514; 2192 -> 2208 pages): continuous sections with columns no
  longer run on in the columns above them. Tests: `pagecols.test.mjs` (balancing, bands, a line or a picture never cut by balancing, the step spy on
  `PageCols.stats.tried`, the frames `balance` tries, a real document's edit against a fresh pagination), `pagepaint.test.mjs` (the
  line).
* **Format > Columns (P10.4, D23, PG27; `SectCols`, `ColumnsBox`: the module row):** the box edits `w:cols` of the
  sections in scope (This section, This point forward, Whole document: `PageValues.scopeOf`, as Page setup).
  Presets as Word makes them: One, Two, Three equal; Left and Right two unequal columns, the narrow one
  floor((text width - 2 spacings) / 3), the wide one 2 narrow + a spacing (Word 12's Columns-Right.docx 8306
  twips, 425 apart: 5395 / 2485; columns1.docx 8312: 2487 / 5399; complex0.docx's 2640 / 5280 on 8640 is another
  rule, taken as hand-edited; P14.1 fix: the narrow one was rounded, so on A4 with 1 inch margins, 9026 twips,
  2529 + 720 + 5778 passed the text by a twip and the box refused Left and Right; floored, 2528 / 5776, the two
  and the spacing never pass the text; test `sectsetup.test.mjs` "Left and Right fit any text width"). Written as Word writes: `w:num` (none for one), `w:sep="1"` only when on,
  `w:space`, and for unequal columns `w:equalWidth="0"` with one `w:col w:w w:space` each (the last without
  `w:space`); a raw `w:cols` (not understood) is dropped when a value is set, kept when nothing is. Number 1..45
  (`MAX_COLS`, PG27); every column at least 0.5 inch (`MIN_COL_TW` 720), equal ones included, so 45 equal columns
  never fit a page of 22 inches: the cap only guards hostile values; unequal widths and spacings no wider than the
  section's text (`SectGeom.geomOf` textW, the gutter counted). This point forward splits the section at the
  caret with a CONTINUOUS break (Word's for columns; Page setup's is next page), none at a section's start.
* **Line numbers (P11.1, D24, PG28, PG29; `LineNumbers`, `PagePaint`):** Print layout only (Draft and Web draw
  none: Word's Draft does not either). A section with a typed `lnNumType` (`PageGalley` `sect(s).lnNumType`; one
  kept raw numbers nothing) numbers its body lines: every line of every root paragraph, empty paragraphs too
  (PG29), but not the lines in a table or a kept block, nor a paragraph with `suppressLineNumbers` in force
  (`FlowDeco.flagOf` over its style layers and own pPr: a style can suppress, `w:val="0"` turns it back on), nor
  anything in a header or footer. A line cut across pages or columns is counted once, where its top is (a frame
  starting with `dy > 0` carries it). The count starts at `start` as written (PG28, the hand-off question: does
  Word write start - 1?; 1 when absent) on the first counted line of a section and, for `restart` `newPage` (the
  default), on the first of each page; `newSection` goes on across the section's pages; `continuous` goes on from
  the last section counted (a section between with no `lnNumType` counts nothing). Shown: n >= 1 and a multiple of
  `countBy` (1 when absent: a `<w:lnNumType/>` with no `w:countBy` numbers every line and the Line numbers box shows it on, Count by 1; owner ruling on review P11 I3: kept, hand-off question CLX1, since Word always writes `w:countBy` and LibreOffice reads a missing one as off), so `start="0"` counts a 0 that is not drawn. Each number is drawn right aligned at
  `distance` (0.25 inch, 360 twips, when absent: Word's Auto) left of its column's left edge (every column of a
  page with columns: its own numbers, the count going on column after column), on the line's baseline, in the
  Line Number character style (`LineNumber`, else a character style named "line number") else Normal's font and
  colour. Cost: a page's own fragments when every numbered section restarts per page; with `newSection` or
  `continuous`, the lines of the pages before by their cursors (no frames built, D7), once per `Pages` object, kept
  per page; P11 fix I2: a `Pages` made from the last one takes over the counts before its pages kept by `PageReuse`
  (`LineNumbers.inherit(P, prev, front)`, called by the `Pages` constructor with `P.kept` after `reuse`: those
  pages and their items are prev's, so the counts are the same), and with no `continuous` restart anywhere a page's
  count is walked from its section's first page (or the page before it, where a continuous break may start it)
  only, FRESH there being the same; the first `numbersOf` after a keystroke on page ~800 of 50,000 paragraphs is
  under 1 ms (`linenumbers-perf.test.mjs`; it was 6-8 ms). The Paragraph box's Suppress line numbers (`ParaPatch` `nolines`) writes `suppressLineNumbers` (typed
  in pPr, `ReadProps`/`WriteProps`, in `OrderP`'s place). The Line numbers box (Format > Layout... > Line numbers..., P11.2: `SectLineNum`, `LineNumBox`)
  sets them on the current section, writing `lnNumType` as Word does and adding the Line Number style once.
* **Floating pictures read (P12.1, D25; `AnchorRead`, `AnchorParts`):** `pictureOf` of a `wp:anchor` picture holds
  `anchor`. `posH.from` is one of `character column margin page insideMargin outsideMargin leftMargin rightMargin`,
  `posV.from` one of `line paragraph margin page topMargin bottomMargin` (D25's lists: a vertical `insideMargin` /
  `outsideMargin` is not understood); each holds exactly one of `align` (H `left center right inside outside`, V
  `top center bottom inside outside`) and `offset` (`wp:posOffset`, EMU, a plain signed 32-bit integer). A
  `wp14:pctPosHOffset` / `pctPosVOffset` is kept as its text in `pct` and not used: Word writes the position in
  `mc:AlternateContent` with a wp14 Choice (the percentage) and a Fallback (an offset), and the Fallback's
  position is taken (else a Choice's own align or offset); a position with only a percentage is not understood.
  `wrap.kind` none / square / tight / through / topAndBottom; `text` (`wrapText` bothSides left right largest)
  for square, tight, through, null otherwise; `dist` the wrap element's `distT/B/L/R` where it has them, else the
  anchor's, else 0; `polygon {edited, points}` for tight and through (`wp:start`, then at least two `wp:lineTo`;
  at most `MAX_POINTS` 4096 points). Flags (`behindDoc`, `allowOverlap`, `layoutInCell`, `locked`) are xsd
  booleans, false when absent; `relativeHeight` 0..2^32-1 (0 absent); `effectExtent` 0s when absent; `simplePos`
  `{on, x, y}`. `unknown` is true when anything is not understood: a value out of range or not a plain integer
  (no spaces, no `+`, no exponent), a `relativeFrom`, `align` or `wrapText` not listed, a missing or repeated
  position or wrap, `simplePos="1"` (placement by simplePos is not done), `hidden="1"`, an attribute other than
  the anchor's own and `wp14:anchorId`/`editId`, a child other than the schema's (and `wp14:sizeRelH/V`, kept,
  not used: the extent is the size), real text. Such a picture is shown at its paragraph as today (inline,
  dashed). Reading never changes the node. Corpus (every file, `WORD_EDIT_CORPUS=1`): 129 anchors in body,
  header and footer parts, none unknown; wrap None in front 66, Square 31, None behind 16, TopAndBottom 16 (the
  spec's regex count: 66 / 30 / 16 / 16; the test allows 2 either way). Final fix B made the count hermetic, as the
  page-start pin (P5.3): the git-ignored `corpus/handoff` files are not counted (Batch D's `cl-*` and `hf-2` files
  had added 12 Square anchors: 42, and the test failed); without the folder 615 files, 104 anchors: in front 51,
  Square 24, behind 13, TopAndBottom 16, the new pin.
* **Floating pictures placed (P12.2, D26; `AnchorPlace`):** in Print layout only (`DocLayout` `floats`, set by
  `WinFit` from the view) an understood anchor (`anchor.unknown` false) is a zero-width item of kind `'anchor'` in
  its line; Draft keeps the picture inline and dashed as before (a view switch re-breaks only the paragraphs that
  may hold one), and so does Print layout for an anchor not understood. Headers and footers lay their stories out
  without `floats`: a float in a header or footer stays inline, dashed (not placed yet). `pg.floats` places, once
  per Page, every anchor on a line the page shows (a cut line continued at a frame's top is the earlier page's; in
  a table, a cell's line where the page shows that part of its row). Horizontal box (`relativeFrom`): `character`
  the anchor's place in its line (width 0); `column` the frame (column) holding the line; `margin` the text area
  (left margin to page width less the right margin, the section's `SectGeom` px); `page`; `leftMargin`,
  `rightMargin`; `insideMargin` the left margin on an odd page and the right on an even one, `outsideMargin` the
  reverse. `align` left / center / right in the box, `inside` left on an odd page and right on an even one,
  `outside` the reverse; else the box's x plus `posOffset` / 9525. Vertical: `paragraph` the anchor paragraph's
  top on the page (its item's top; begun on an earlier page or column: its first line there; own reading: the
  space before is inside), `line` the anchor's line, `margin` (top margin to page height less the bottom margin,
  the section's margins: a header that pushes the body does not move it), `page`, `topMargin`, `bottomMargin`;
  `align` top / center / bottom (`inside` read as top, `outside` as bottom: own reading); else the box's y plus
  the offset. Kept on the page (PG30): a float whose bottom is below the page's moves up to end there, then one
  above the top moves down to 0 (taller than the page: its top at 0); x is never moved. `layoutInCell` in a
  cell: every horizontal box but `character` and `page` and every vertical one but `paragraph`, `line` and `page`
  is the cell's text area (own reading of "positioned in the cell"; in a nested table the innermost cell's x and
  width, the root row's height). The extent is the size (never fitted to the column); `effectExtent` is not used
  for placement. `paintPage` draws the `behindDoc` floats first, under the text, the others after the header and
  footer, over everything, each group by `relativeHeight` (equal: document order). Text wraps round them since
  P12.3 (below). `PicFind` finds a placed float where it is drawn (`picAt`: the
  floats in front first, the top one first, then pictures in lines, then the floats behind text where the point is on no text of a line (P12a fix I2: a click on text over a picture behind it puts the caret there, as Word's; the picture is selected where there is no text, or from the keyboard, Shift+arrow over its anchor); `selectedPic`
  of its anchor's offset): its rect the box on the page, its item the anchor item as kind `'pic'` with the
  float's `pic` (`floating` true), so a click selects it, its handles are drawn there and a drag on one beeps as
  before (moving and resizing it: P12.5).
* **Text wrap (P12.3, D27; `LineShape`, `WrapPass`; settled page by page: P12a fix C1):** in Print layout only.
  Each placed float whose wrap is Square, Tight, Through or TopAndBottom is an EXCLUSION on its page
  (`LineShape.exclusionsOf`, the one rule): Square its box plus `distT/B/L/R` (EMU / 9525); TopAndBottom the same,
  and no text beside it on its lines (the whole frame width); Tight and Through (the same) the `wrapPolygon` scaled
  from 21600 units across the extent, each line band getting the polygon's own x extent over the band plus
  `distL/R` (no `distT/B`, as the schema: a polygon of fewer than 3 or more than 4096 points, or a coordinate not
  finite, gives the box); wrapNone (in front of text, behind text) never excludes. A line gets ONE interval (PG31:
  Word puts text on both sides of a centred float when both are wide enough; deferred, OD9): `bothSides` and
  `largest` the widest gap the exclusions leave, `left` the gap left of the float, `right` the gap right of it; a
  gap under 48 px (`MIN_FREE`) is no room: the line moves down below the band (`shape.next`), at most 64 times
  (`MAX_SKIP`). An exclusion counts for a line where it overlaps the line's band (a band that only touches it,
  within 0.01 px, does not: P12a fix C1) and the paragraph's text width. Each line is tried at ITS OWN height
  (`LineFit.fitLines`: a taller line, an inline picture, does not reach under a float; a shorter one is not moved
  past a band it does not reach). A paragraph's first line that starts its frame is not moved below the frame's
  bottom (it could go on no other page: it stays, text under the float); the px a band moves a first line down
  are not its space before (`LineFit.beforeOf`), so a page's top keeps them. Which paragraphs:
  `WrapPass.wrapPass(L, P, upTo)` (pure), run by the window as `ColPass` (`ViewPass.wrapStep`: after an edit up to
  the caret's page at once, within 40 ms, the rest in the slices), one more layout a pass with `DocLayout` opts
  `wrap` (`dw.wrap`, `WinFit`; Draft and Web none). A paragraph's PARTS: one per frame of the page where its lines
  meet an exclusion of that page in the frame's width (`WrapWant`), holding ONLY the exclusions that meet them
  (P12a fix M2), relative to its top and the frame's left to 1/100 px, with the frame's ys as a window when it
  shows in more than one frame; its wrap KEY is the parts' sigs, and `DocItems` keeps its lines only when the key
  is `prev`'s (or comes back: `ItemReuse.swapAlt`). Pages are SETTLED IN ORDER, each from the same start whatever
  came before (P12a fix C1, the rulings: edited == fresh):
  - a page whose inputs are not those of its record (`WrapMemo`: its start, the inputs of its items, its
    geometry, the parts its paragraphs have from other pages) starts again: its paragraphs keep only their parts
    for the pages before, and those after it none (kept aside, given back once it settles, so pages after it that
    are the same need not settle again);
  - its paragraphs then get the parts they want, guessed TOP DOWN (`WrapGuess`: a paragraph re-broken with its new
    parts moves the paragraphs below it, and the floats anchored there with a paragraph or line position, by the
    height it gained), so a cascade of k floats down a page settles in a pass or two, not k;
  - a settled page whose end moves later (a paragraph its wrap sent to the next page would come back there, where
    it is not wrapped) keeps its end: the item after it is PINNED to start a page (`PageGalley` `breakBefore`), as
    Word keeps a page laid out (PG32: the review's oscillation fixture ends with the paragraph on page 2, no text
    under the float, the same after any keystroke);
  - a page that comes back to a state it had, or has not settled after 16 passes (`MAX_PASSES`): when the end of
    one of its columns moved (a paragraph that its wrap splits across two columns and its unwrapped self does
    not, P12a fix I3), that paragraph is KEPT WHOLE (a pin `'k:'`: `PageGalley` `keepLines`) as Word lays a
    column out once; else, when its end moved, it is pinned at the first end it had (once); else laid out
    IGNORING WRAP (deterministic: text may run under a float there) until its inputs change.
  A float across two newspaper columns wraps the lines of both: each column's paragraphs get a part for their
  frame (`wrap-cols.test.mjs`, `word-wrap.mjs`).
  A page settled is looked at no more while its paragraphs' parts are the very ones (`WrapPage`). Text in a
  table's CELL wraps round the floats anchored in that cell, within the cell (P12a fix I5, D27: `WrapCells`, the
  cell's paragraphs placed by `AnchorPlace.cellsOn`, parts as root paragraphs' with their table's id; `DocStack`
  breaks a cell's paragraph with its shape; `DocItems` keeps no table whole whose cells' keys changed,
  `WrapPass.cellKey`; no guess top down: plain passes); a float in a cell never wraps the root paragraphs, nor
  another cell's text. A table and a kept block stay as they are beside a float; a list label stays at its
  indent. Floats in headers and footers are not placed (P12.2) and do not wrap the body (D13,
  PG13). Measured (`wrap-settle.test.mjs`, Node): 3 to 10 alternating floats a page, no line under a float,
  edited == fresh; 2,000 paragraphs each with a float (125 pages): 373 passes, about 0.55 s, no line under a float;
  the corpus file `hyperlink/632399964516872542 1.docx` (16 top-and-bottom charts): no line under a chart, a
  keystroke on page 18 about 4 ms (median of 20, budget 15 ms); a seeded fuzz of hostile documents and edits:
  edited == fresh; 100 pages with a float on each (`lineshape.test.mjs`): a keystroke beside the float on page
  51 about 2 ms, only that page's paragraphs broken again.
* **Floating tables placed (P12.6, owner ruling R5; `TblFloat`, `AnchorPlace`/`AnchorTbl`, `PageFill.floatSpan`):**
  in Print layout only, a ROOT table whose `tblPr` holds a `w:tblpPr` that `TblFloat.floatOf` understands, no
  taller than its page's frame, is placed on its page like a floating picture: it takes no height in the flow
  (the galley is unchanged: pagination skips its span as it skips a section band), is never split by
  `PageRows`, and goes whole on the page its place in the flow falls on. Horizontal: `horzAnchor` text the
  frame (column) holding it, margin the text area, page the page; `tblpXSpec` left / center / right in it,
  inside / outside by the page's parity (as pictures); else the box's x plus `tblpX` / 15 px. Vertical:
  `vertAnchor` text its own place in the flow, margin and page as pictures; `tblpYSpec` top / center / bottom,
  inside as top, outside as bottom, inline the box's top (own reading); else plus `tblpY` / 15. A spec wins over
  the offset. The table's box (its left edge as drawn, `it.x + it.left`, its width and height) is what is placed
  (own reading: `tblInd` and `jc` do not move it). Kept on the page (PG30) as pictures. A table that
  would overlap a floating table placed before it on the page moves down below it (again until none), then PG30
  (with no room below it may overlap: own reading), when EITHER of the two has `tblOverlap` never (ECMA-376
  17.4.56: whether other floating tables may overlap this one; P12b fix I3), or when its top left is the other's
  (it would be hidden: P12b fix I4). Its Float `{tbl, x, y, w, h, behind: false, z: -1,
  cell: false, tfloat, bx, by}` comes first among the floats over the text (under every picture float drawn over
  the text); text wraps round it (P12.7, next bullet). Its fragment (`PrintFrags`: `float`, `dx`, `dy` to the Float,
  no clip) is drawn with the text there with no dashed outline, and the caret, hits (`PrintHit`: a placed table
  first, where it is drawn), selection boxes and every table command work as in any table. Pictures anchored in
  its cells are placed as in any table, moved with it. NOT placed, in the flow as before, with the dashed outline
  (`TablePaint.outline`, in Print layout too): a floating table in a cell, in a header or footer story (laid out
  without floats), with anything `TblFloat` does not understand (`unknown`), taller than its page's frame, and in
  Draft and Web layout. Moving or resizing a floating table by dragging is not in this batch (R5). Tests:
  `tblfloat.test.mjs`, `anchorplace.test.mjs` (floating tables), `pagerows.test.mjs` (never split).
* **Text wraps round floating tables; editing inside them (P12.7, owner ruling R5; `LineExcl`, `WrapGuess`,
  `TblDrag`):** a placed floating table is a SQUARE exclusion (`LineShape.exclusionsOf`, the one rule: its box
  widened by `leftFromText` / `rightFromText` / `topFromText` / `bottomFromText`, twips / 15, each the room kept
  between the table's edge and the nearest text on that side), with text on both sides read as one interval a
  line, the larger side (OD9), and a band with under half an inch free skipped as for pictures. It takes part in
  the same page-by-page wrap passes as pictures (`WrapPass`; a floating table is in `L.anchored`,
  `ItemReuse.anchored`, also when the layout before had no floats: from Draft, `DocItems`), keyed by the
  exclusions, so a table that grows as you type in it re-breaks only the paragraphs beside it on its page; the top
  down guess (`WrapGuess`) moves a table placed from its flow place (vertAnchor text) by the height gained above
  it. Inside it everything works as in any table: the caret and typing, Tab, every Table command, Up and Down in
  and out of it in document order (`SelTable`), undo (the Doc deep-equal, the earlier line breaks back). Its borders
  drag as in any table, its OUTLINE (its right edge, its last row's bottom) too (P12b fix I2, owner ruling: as
  Word; the drag never changes its position, `tblpPr`), found where it is DRAWN (`PlacePrint.floatAt`, before the
  flow) and never at its place in the galley (`PlacePrint.placed`: a press on the text there finds no edge of it;
  `TblEdge`, `TblDrag`). A floating table in a header
  or footer is not placed and wraps nothing (D13). Tests: `lineshape.test.mjs` (floating tables: the exclusion,
  left / right / fromText, under half an inch, two tables, header, Draft, from Draft to Print layout, typing in a
  cell == fresh and undone, 100 pages a keystroke in a cell about 2 ms; corpus-gated: every file with a floating
  table settles, no line under a table), `word-wrap.mjs` (floating tables).
* **Floating tables: the P12b fix wave.** C1: a table placed from its flow place (vertAnchor text) moves with
  the lines above it, and those lines wrap round it when it reaches up to them (a small negative `tblpY`): they
  grow, move it down, leave it and come back, a cycle. On a cycle the page first HOLDS such tables where its
  first pass had them (the page's start: the lines above unwrapped there; `WrapPage`, the wrap's `tys`), so only
  those tables leave their flow place, and the page settles again; nothing on it is laid out ignoring wrap for
  that. Tests: `tblfloat-wrap.test.mjs` (tblpY -150; a sweep of tblpY -3000..3000 step 30: no page falls, no
  line under the table). I1: edited == fresh with tables and pictures together. A page's passes may hold more
  items than it ends with (its first pass has the lines on it unwrapped), and its record depends on them: a page
  remembered as settled is looked at again when one of those items changed (before, an edit there was missed:
  pictures alone too). Only the tables on the page are held; a page whose record is still valid holds them again
  when they were dropped while it was away. Test: `tblfloat-wrap.test.mjs` (a seeded fuzz of 200 documents of
  floating tables and pictures, 6 edits each: edited == fresh, no page laid out ignoring wrap; the same seeds'
  pictures alone: seeds 20, 58). A paragraph cut at the page's end in some passes and whole in others (its
  picture's line going to the next page and back) is kept whole, as one flipping between two columns was (P12a
  fix I3), before the page is pinned or laid out ignoring wrap. I2: a press on ordinary text never starts a drag of a floating table's border:
  `TblEdge.edgeAt` looks for a placed table's edges where it is drawn (its box widened by the 3 screen px), then in
  the flow leaving placed tables out; every border of a placed table drags (the outline is no longer refused).
  Tests: `tblfloat-place.test.mjs` (I2), `word-wrap.mjs` (the outline dragged). I3: `tblOverlap` never on
  either table keeps a later table off an earlier one (`AnchorTbl`). I4: floating tables are never hidden under
  each other: a table whose top left is that of one placed before it moves below it, overlap allowed or not
  (tables in a row at one flow place are stacked); in pagination such a stack of tables placed from their flow
  place goes on the next page from the table whose stacked bottom would pass the frame (`PageFill`); the new part
  of a Split Table and a floating table pasted in its own document get `<w:tblOverlap w:val="never"/>` (after
  their `tblpPr`, in place of any `tblOverlap` they had: `TblFloat.apart`), so they never overlap the table they
  came from; the original keeps its elements byte for byte, and a table from another document comes as it was.
  Tests: `tblfloat-place.test.mjs` (I3, I4), `anchorplace.test.mjs`. I5: a placed table is kept on the sheet
  across too (pictures are not: a table holds text to edit): its drawn x at least 0 and at most the page's width
  less its first column's, so its left cell is on the sheet (`tblpPr` unchanged). Tests: `tblfloat-place.test.mjs`
  (I5). Minor: a raw element of an edited part is written as read to the space before its `/>` (WimpLib
  `XmlParse` / `XmlWrite` `sp`), so an edited floating table's `tblpPr` and `tblOverlap` come back byte for byte
  from a LibreOffice file too (`clearing-break-with-fly.docx`). Tests: `xml.test.mjs`, `tblfloat.test.mjs`. A
  table placed from its flow place (vertAnchor text) whose bottom there (with its `tblpY`) would pass the frame
  goes whole to the next page with the text after it (`PageFill`; a first one on its page that still would ends
  at the frame's bottom, `AnchorTbl`): never over the bottom margin and footer, nor moved up over the text above
  it (that fed the wrap back, a cycle across two pages). Any `tblpYSpec` with vertAnchor text is read as top (the box has no height: center,
  bottom and outside would put it over the text before it; Word writes none of them). A universal measure in
  `tblpPr` ("1in") is not read: unknown, in the flow. Tests: `tblfloat-place.test.mjs` (Minor), `pagerows.test.mjs`.
  The wrap engine (found by the fuzz): a page's record also holds the inputs of the item after its end each pass
  (the one that did not fit decides where it ends: an edit there starts the page again, `WrapMemo`), and only a
  paragraph's cut at the page's end counts as flipping (`WrapPins`); the fuzz asserts every settle takes fewer
  than 64 passes (the guard never reached).
* **Wrap text commands (P12.4, D28; `WrapCmd`, `WrapXml`, `WrapMenu`):** Format > Wrap text > (after
  Picture...; shaded unless a picture is selected) In line with text, Square, Tight, Top and bottom, Behind
  text, In front of text, the picture's kind ticked (none for Through or an anchor not understood). Each choice
  is one undo step (one `replaceText` of the picture's U+FFFC); the same kind again changes nothing. In line ->
  floating builds a `wp:anchor` with Word's defaults: horizontal `column` offset = the picture's x in its
  column now (its line item's x), vertical `paragraph` offset 0, `distT/B` 0, `distL/R` 114300, `relativeHeight`
  the document's largest + 1 (body and stories, at most 4294967295), `behindDoc` for Behind text,
  `allowOverlap` and `layoutInCell` 1, `simplePos` 0 0, Tight's polygon the extent's rectangle. Floating -> in
  line keeps `docPr` (id, alt text), `extent`, `effectExtent`, `cNvGraphicFramePr` and `a:graphic`. Between wrap
  kinds only the wrap element and `behindDoc` change (a Tight or Through polygon is kept for Tight; `wrapText`
  kept). A floating picture whose anchor is not understood (`unknown`: drawn inline and dashed) is refused
  with a beep. The result is written in schema order (`wrapcmd.test.mjs` checks with xmllint and `wml.xsd`).
  Own readings: Behind/In front set `behindDoc` too (Word does); a Square made from Tight starts with the anchor's
  dist again (the wrap element's own dist attributes are not carried over); with no float in the document the
  new `relativeHeight` is 1.
* **Known gaps:** a page break that ends the last paragraph of a section (not the document) followed by a
  page-starting section gives no empty page between them (the same question, PG40); a continuous section that starts part way down a page has no `first` page
  (no number restart, no first-page header: P7 fix I2, hand-off question HFX1); `vAlign` is the section of the
  page's first item.

## Fields (Batch D): the rules

Batch D P8.1-P8.4, P9.1 (D15-D19). The model keeps every field as it was read; nothing on the screen writes a stored
result (OD3): only Edit > Update field and Edit > Update all fields (P9.1, `FieldCmd`) do.

* **What is computed (D18).** A field whose evaluator (`Fields.REGISTRY`) is page-dependent (PAGE, NUMPAGES,
  SECTIONPAGES, SECTION) or volatile (DATE, TIME), not locked (`w:fldLock`), with its result in one paragraph (the
  separate and the end fldChar there; a `w:fldSimple`'s own U+FFFC) is shown computed (`FieldShow.computedIn`). Every
  other field (no evaluator: MERGEFIELD, IF ...; PAGEREF and TOC, which have one from Batch E3 but are shown stored, and STYLEREF in the body; non-volatile: AUTHOR, FILENAME, CREATEDATE, SEQ, REF ...; locked;
  a result across paragraphs; fields inside kept nodes) shows its stored result and is edited as text, as before.
* **Drawn as one token.** `LineTokens` asks the layout's `fieldText(para, off)` at each `w:fldChar` and `w:fldSimple`
  inline (a paragraph with none asks nothing) and draws the result range `[from, to)` as ONE shown 'w' token of the
  computed text (no break inside it) in the format of the result's first run, or the separate fldChar's when the
  result is empty. The item carries `field {b, e}` (the begin offset when in the paragraph, else null; the end's).
  The stored text is drawn the same way when there is no value (no `now`; no page: Draft view), so the caret rules
  do not depend on the view.
  P8 fix I2: the results go in in ONE merge pass over the tokens (a result nested in another result shown is left
  out) and `fieldText` finds the show by offset in a Map, so a paragraph of 10,000 PAGE or DATE fields, or their
  codes, lays out in tens of ms, linear in the fields (`fields-linear.test.mjs`; it was quadratic: 35 s).
* **The values.** `L.fields` (a `DocLayout` option, carried from prev): `{now}` from the window (`dw.fields`, the
  time it was opened, or of its last field command, P9 fix I2: DATE and TIME), a story layout's `page` and `pages`, the body's `pageOf` and `pages`. NUMPAGES
  and SECTIONPAGES count `countsOf(P)`: the Pages once done, before that the last finished Pages' (`P.counts`, D7:
  the previous count), and the stored result when none has finished (a document just opened).
* **Headers and footers (D13).** A page paints its header and footer through `PageHF.layoutOf(ref, s, pg, P)`: the
  story laid out with the page's values, memoised by `StoryLayout` under the values key `FieldShow.storyKey` (the
  page-dependent values joined; '' for a story without them), so pages with the same values share one layout: a
  1,500-page document with PAGE in the footer lays out one footer per page PAINTED, none for the others. The heights
  pagination uses come from the layout without a page (the stored results). When the slices finish the window is
  drawn again, so NUMPAGES shows the new count at once (`fieldshow.test.mjs`: under 50 ms). The header and footer
  mode's editing layout is made again when its page's values change (`HdrEdit`).
* **Body text (PG20).** The galley lays a paragraph out with the values it knows: its page from the last pass
  (`pageOf`), else none (the stored result). After each new Pages (and when the slices finish, or when the pages
  are all worked out already as `placeView` ends: a short document is paginated by the info line's count, with
  no slice to look; P8 fix I1, `word-fields.mjs`) `ViewMode` asks
  `FieldPass.passOf`: a root paragraph whose page-dependent value differs on the page now worked out for it gets one
  more layout (`dw.newLayout` with the new `pageOf`; `DocItems` does not adopt those paragraphs, `relayOf`, and keeps
  every other line). One per paragraph per edit (`tries`): if that layout moves it to a page where the value differs
  again, the difference is left until the next edit (Word repaginates the same way). A paragraph in a table cell
  shows its stored page values. Draft view shows the values last worked out in Print layout.
* **One unit for the caret and the keys (PG21; Review Focus 3).** Left and Right step over a computed result in
  one press (`SelMove`: to after its end fldChar, or before its begin); a click lands at the nearer edge of the whole
  field, before its begin fldChar or after its end (`PosLine.offIn`, P8 fix M4: before, the result's start, just
  after the separate, was inside the field). Backspace or Delete that would take a character of it selects the result instead
  (`EditDel`, `FieldEdit.resultIn`); a second press, or typing, Enter, a paste or an Insert command over a selection
  that takes part of a result without the whole field, is refused (a beep; Cut copies but deletes nothing). Text
  typed at a result's edge goes before or after the whole field (`FieldEdit.typingAt`). A selection from before the
  field to after it (Shift+Right) deletes the whole field. Word lets the result be edited and replaces it at the
  next update; here it is refused. A fldSimple is one U+FFFC: its result is selected first, then deleted whole.
* **No half fields (P8 fix I3).** A range that takes some of a complex field's marks (begin, separate, end) and not
  the others is made whole before it is deleted, typed over (Enter, Insert commands too), cut or pasted over
  (`FieldEdit.whole`, through `guard`, `EditDel` and `ClipPaste.cutSelection`): from the field's begin to after its
  end, for EVERY field (computed or not: REF, TOC, MERGEFIELD; across paragraphs), again until no field is cut;
  Word does the same. The computed-result refusal above then applies to the range made whole (a range taking part
  of a result and no mark is still refused). Copy takes the range as it is; a paste drops the marks with no
  partner among the pasted blocks (`FieldPair.paired`: a separate or end with no begin open, a begin never ended
  and its separate and instrText). `fields-balance.test.mjs`: the cases, and 200 seeded runs of 30 random edits
  near field marks in the body, a header, a footer and a table cell leave every part's fldChars balanced and undo
  of everything gives the bytes opened (the reviewer's run found 306 unbalanced parts before).
* **Cost (D37).** `FieldScan` is memoised per paragraph and per block list; `FieldShow` per scan. A keystroke in a
  paragraph without a fldChar or fldSimple runs no field code (`fieldshow.test.mjs` spies on `FieldMarks.work` and
  `FieldShow.work`), in Draft and in Print layout. P8 fix M1: nor does it walk the records of the paragraphs with
  fields: `FieldPass.carry` shares the last layout's record map, and `passOf` looks only at new records and those
  on the pages that are new objects (all of them when the page count changes; `fieldpass-cost.test.mjs`). A keystroke in a paragraph with a field scans the document's block list once (the scan memo is keyed by
  `doc.sections` at the doc's `DocVersion`, P9.1 fix: before it a body edit was not seen).
* **Field codes (P8.4, D18).** View > Field codes or Shift+F9 (per window, not kept; F9 stays Redo, R2) sets
  `dw.fields.codes` and lays the document out again (`FieldView.setCodes`). `FieldShow.fieldText` then gives, at a
  field's begin, its code (`FieldCodes.codeAt`: `{ PAGE }`, a nested field as its own `{ ... }`) drawn as ONE token
  over the whole field (begin to end + 1, `field {b, e}`: the caret steps over it as over a computed result), and
  nothing for a field inside one; a field spanning paragraphs shows as without the codes. Headers and footers follow
  (`StoryLayout` compares `codes`). Display only: the model, the editing rules (`FieldEdit`) and the bytes written are
  as before (`word-fields.mjs`: saved in the codes view, every part as saved showing the results).
* **Field shading (P8.4, D18).** View > Field shading > Never / When selected (default) / Always, the app's choice in
  Choices:Letters (`'fieldShading'`, every window at once). `ItemPaint` paints `#d8d8d8` the full line height behind
  the items `FieldShade.shadeOf` gives: a field's result (with the codes shown, the whole code), for When selected
  only while the selection touches the field (the caret just before or after a computed result counts). Read at
  paint time from `dw.fields.shade` (getters): a choice or a caret move needs no layout. Fields across paragraphs
  are not shaded.
* **Update (P9.1, D19, R2).** Edit > Update field (the fields at the caret, just before or after a field counting,
  or touching the selection, and the fields inside them; in the header and footer mode every field of the story,
  with the mode's page) and Edit > Update all fields (the body; shaded in the mode). No key: F9 stays Redo. Each
  field with an evaluator, no lock and a value (`Fields.evaluate`; page fields once every page is worked out, the
  page the field's begin is on; in Draft pages are made for it) gets the value as its stored result (`FieldCmd`,
  `FieldPut`): the first result run's format, or with `\* MERGEFORMAT` per character (PG22); a result across
  paragraphs merged into one; a field with no separate given one; a fldSimple a new node. Left exactly as read: no
  evaluator (IF, MERGEFIELD ...: an `IF { PAGE }` gets only its inner PAGE updated; PAGEREF, SEQ, REF and the rest of Batch E3's are updated here too, a TOC by `FieldPasses` as a whole), locked, a result
  holding anything but text (another field, a bookmark...), a result across cells or around a table, a field inside
  a kept node. One undo step; nothing evaluable: a beep and no step; every value already stored: no step. Saving
  never updates (`fields-update.test.mjs`: a PAGE shown 3 is saved 1). The corpus pass updates every field of every
  body and story and checks each field without an evaluator (and nothing evaluable inside) identical inline by
  inline, and undo back to the document read.
* **Insert (P9.2, D19, PG23).** Insert > Page number, Number of pages, Date, Time put in `PAGE`, `NUMPAGES`,
  `DATE \@ "dd/MM/yyyy"`, `TIME \@ "HH:mm"`, each `\* MERGEFORMAT`; Insert > Field... (`FieldBox`) any code. A new
  field is begin, ONE instrText `" CODE "` (`xml:space="preserve"`), separate, its result, end, in the caret's run
  format, the result filled at once (an unknown name: empty), one undo step, the caret after it; in the header and
  footer mode in its story (a PAGE in a footer shows each page's number). With the selection in a field the box edits
  its code (the instrText inlines replaced by one; a fldSimple's `w:instr`) and updates its result; a code holding
  another field is refused (PG23), and so is a field put in another field's code.

* **User guide (P9.4, R4).** Part 12 of `$.Docs.Letters`, "Headers, footers and fields": what the pages show
  (distances, a tall header pushing the text, the kept-part grey band, first / even / default and "Same as previous",
  a continuous section starting mid-page having no first page: HFX1), the mode (double-click or View > Header and
  footer, from Draft too; the pale body, the tab labels, the info line; every text command works, breaks shaded,
  Page setup and Layout shaded; clicks across pages and stories, Escape and the body double-click; a page with no
  header made on the first key, one step with the typing; typing in a linked header edits the chain, `chainStart`),
  the Header menu (every item; Link to previous on deletes the section's own story WITHOUT Word's question, review
  P7 M4; off copies the inherited one), undo and redo moving between stories (`HdrStep`; Draft stays in the body),
  Find and Replace in the mode story-only (review P7 M3), the fields computed and when (Draft the last values,
  NUMPAGES the previous count while counting, cell paragraphs stored), the fields never evaluated or treated as text
  (no evaluator, locked, across paragraphs, inside kept nodes: hyperlinks, content controls, tracked insertions;
  review P8 M3), the atomic result (arrows, the click at the nearer edge, Backspace selecting, typing at the edges,
  refusals), no half fields (whole on delete / type over / cut / paste over; Copy as selected, the paste dropping
  orphans), Update field / Update all fields (the mode: the story's fields with its page; Update all shaded; saving
  never updates; no key, F9 stays Redo, R2), Insert (pointer to part 8), codes and shading (and what they do not
  show), the own defaults still to check (header heights, TIME HH:mm, the stamp picture, odd number formats) and the
  gaps (no headers in Draft; heights from stored text; cell page fields; no Link question). Parts 2 (the field row,
  the band double-click, the stale "not drawn" sentence), 3 (keys: Shift+F9, Update field without a key; undo across
  stories), 4 and 5 ("Not possible yet"), 9 (header pictures shown), 11 (the band row, the Layout box, How close),
  16 (headers and fields kept: stored results until Update), 19 (fields never run; INCLUDETEXT / INCLUDEPICTURE never
  fetched; DDE and merge never reach anything), 20 and 22 are brought up to date; `!Help` has a "Headers and footers"
  paragraph and the README a **Headers, footers and fields:** paragraph.

## Styles (Batch E1): what changed in existing modules

The new modules are in the module table (`StyleId` to `ThemeRead`). Existing modules changed as follows.

* `Styles`: the Based on chain is cut at the exported `MAX_CHAIN` = 100 styles (the style itself and 99 ancestors, the farthest dropped; cycle-safe), pinned by `styles.test.mjs` (the style itself and 99 ancestors: the 100th STYLE is the last one followed). `StyleTable.theme` (from `ThemeRead`) is set by `DocxRead` (`styles.theme`, only when the theme part exists).
* `ReadStyles` / `WriteStyles`: `Style.attrs` keeps the other attributes of the `w:style` element (`[[name, value]]`), so a style rebuilt after an edit still has them; foreign attributes named `type`, `default`, `customStyle` or `styleId` are kept on a rebuilt style. A changed style has `raw: null` and is rebuilt from its fields and `extra`.
* `FormatSet` re-exports `charCommand` (now in `FormatChar`), `applyStyle` and `updateToMatch` (`StyleApply`).
* `Format.query` returns `charStyle` (the id of the character style of the selected characters, `''` for none, null when they differ) next to `style`.
* `FormatEff.charOf` and the font name honour the theme (`styles.theme`): theme fonts and colours (`w:color` themeColor, tint, shade) are shown as Word does, in layout, the toolbar's font field and copied HTML.
* `ParaBox` exports `coreRows`, `paraChange`, `adapt`, `kindOf` and `WRITABLE`, the alignment to line-spacing rows shared with `StyleBox`.
* `FormatTabs.tabsFor(doc, p, arg)` and `ListMake.listFor(doc, e)` take any `{pStyle?, pPr}` / a gallery entry, so a style (`StyleTarget`) can be the target of the Tabs box and the number galleries.
* `StylesBuiltin.galleryIds()`: the built-ins Word's gallery offers (Normal, Title, List Paragraph, Heading 1 to 6), listed as latent styles by `StyleList` and added by `StyleCmd.ensureBuiltin` on first use; `StylesBuiltin.isBuiltinStyle(style)` (the id is a built-in's, or the stored name is one of Word's built-in names, `StyleName.isBuiltinName`: a German file's Normal is `Standard`) is what `StyleCmd`, `StylePatch` and `StylesState` use to refuse deleting or renaming one; `deleteStyle` also refuses the default style of its type. `ensureBuiltin` clears `isDefault` on a style it adds when the type already has a default.
* `FormatMenu`: Style > (`StyleMenu`) and Styles...; `ToolbarBind` shows the character style's name or the paragraph's (Word's names) and opens `StyleMenu`; `KeymapMore` / `DocKeys` `styleList` = Ctrl+Shift+S.

To check in real Word: the hand-off files `st-1-created.docx` to `st-8-latent.docx` and `st-README.txt` (`node tests/moreapps/handoff-styles.mjs`, written to the git-ignored `tests/moreapps/corpus/handoff/`; questions ST1.., priority list first) have NOT yet been opened in real Word.

## Footnotes and endnotes (Batch E2): what changed in existing modules

The new modules are in the module table (`NoteRead` to `EndnoteLayout`). The user's side is `$.Docs.Letters` part 24.

### The model

* `doc.notes` (`Model.emptyNotes()`; absent in a Doc made elsewhere means empty) is `{footnotes, endnotes, root, prolog, order, raw, read}`: `footnotes` and `endnotes` are `Map<int id, Note>`; `root`, `prolog`, `order`, `raw` and `read` are each keyed `{footnotes, endnotes}` (`root` `{name, attrs}`, `prolog` `{decl, before, after}`, `order` the ids in the file's order, `raw` the odd root children `[{at, node}]`, `read` the snapshot of what was read, so `NoteWrite` tells an untouched part, written as its bytes, from a changed one). The names `rootF`/`rootE`/`prologF`/`prologE` of the first design were not used. `meta.noteParts {footnotes?, endnotes?}` names the modelled parts. A part the reader cannot model (bad XML, a cap, a `w:sectPr`, a wrong root) stays in `doc.parts` as bytes.
* A mark is an inline `{kind: 'noteRef', note: 'footnote' \| 'endnote', id, custom?, customNode?, self?, node}` (`ReadPara`, `WritePara`). It is modelled only where the caller says so (`ReadBody`, `TblRead` through `ctx.notes` at every depth, `NoteRead`); in headers, footers, text boxes and other raw containers it stays a raw inline (the grey box). A mark with `w:customMarkFollows` is tied to the next `w:t` of its run (`custom`, with the original element kept as `customNode` and written back verbatim); with no plain text following it stays raw. An id must be 0..2^31-1 digits else the mark is raw. `self` is a note's own mark (`w:footnoteRef`). `ModelCheck.checkNotes` (called from the `DocxWrite` check) checks the maps, `order` against the keys, and `noteRef` (a `customNode` text must equal `custom`). `readDocx` has an internal switch `noteMarks: false` giving the earlier behaviour (tests).
* `noteState(doc, 'footnotes' \| 'endnotes')` (`NoteNumbers`): `known`, `unknown` (the part is bytes only: its marks are counted, no new note is taken, a paste's marks are dropped with a notice, `OpsNotes` refuses with "could not be read ... takes no new note", Convert refuses) or `missing` (no part: marks show `[?]` until `NoteParts.ensure` makes one).
* Ids. `nextNoteId(doc, kind)` is max + 1 over the Map, the raw nodes' `w:id` and the marks of that kind in the body, headers and footers, at least 1, and throws RangeError at `MAX_NOTE_ID` (999,999,999; a hostile mark beyond it is not counted, so it cannot block inserts). It is not a session high-water mark: after an undo of an insert the same id is taken again (pinned in `opsnotes.test.mjs`; the first design said ids were never reused: accepted as it is, since a pasted mark always gets a fresh id at paste time, so a reused id never names a note a mark still points at). Block ids (`Walk.scanStories`, so `reserveIds`, `OpsUtil.checkIds`), picture `docPr` ids (`PicIds`), list `numId`s (`ListUsed`), `sdt` ids (`StoryCopy`), anchor z (`WrapCmd`) and bookmark ids (`BookmarkMarks.noteMarks`, used by `Bookmarks.addBookmark` next to the body's marks and `storyMarks`) all see the body, the headers and footers, and every note, from the body, a header facade or a note facade. Bookmark NAMES are only checked within one part, so a name can repeat between the body and a note (as already between the body and a header).

### Ops, undo and the facade

* Ops are in `OpsNotes`. A note's blocks are edited through the story key `story: {note: {kind, id}}` (`ModelCheck` `opStory`/`noteKeyOf`, own properties only; `OpsPath` `locate`/`own`/`inStory`). The facade key is the same form: `facadeOf(d, {note: {kind, id}})` gives a `NoteFacade` (a `StoryFacade` subclass, memoised under a NUL-prefixed key) whose view is one section holding the note's blocks, with `stories` = the headers and footers plus the body as a story. `setDocPart rels` becomes `setNoteRels`; `refuses()` includes footnote and endnote (no note in a note); section ops and a removed note raise RangeError. Every existing command runs on it unchanged (typing, Enter, formatting, lists, pictures, Find (that note only), undo).
* The facade's `relsOp` (shared by the header and the note facade; it returns null, so no op and no undo step, when the main part already has every document-level relationship added and the story's own are as they were) re-makes in the real document's `document.xml.rels` the relationships a story's `setDocPart rels` ADDS that are document-level kinds (styles, numbering, settings, fontTable, theme, footnotes, endnotes, comments, ... found from the MAIN part's relationships, ECMA-376 11.3). This was a deliberate bug fix that also fixed lists made in headers and footers: before, the first list made in a story of a document with no numbering part put the numbering relationship in the header's own `.rels`, where Word does not look. External relationships, images, hyperlinks and unknown kinds stay part-local. The classification table is in the `StoryFacade` header. `storyfacade.test.mjs` pins the old behaviour's replacement.
* `NoteKeep` at the end of each outermost undo step: there is no single place where text is deleted (Backspace/Delete, `deleteRange`, table commands, Find/Replace, paste, typing over a selection, Outline moves... each build their own ops), so `Document.groupEnd` (outermost only) asks `NoteKeep.dropped(doc, invs)` for a `removeNotes` op and applies it INTO THE SAME GROUP: undo brings marks, notes and numbers back together. `apply` outside a group now runs as a one-op group. A refused removal is swallowed (the edit stands and the note stays as an orphan: an edit is never lost). Orphans and separators are never removed. Zero cost for a document with no note.
* Copy-on-write: a note op replaces `doc.notes` with a new object and the changed kind's Map with a new Map, so a keystroke in a note costs a Map copy (about 0.45 ms at 10,000 notes; body typing is O(1)). Undo restores the old `Note` objects, so the layout re-keys on undo. Bulk work uses the linear ops: `removeNotes`/`addNotes` for deleting many marks, and Convert all is one bulk op (10,000 notes in about 90 ms).
* `NoteParts.ensure` and its Word assumptions are in the module row. `EditStep.stepTo` understands note keys and `HdrStep.afterChange` sends a step deciding in a note to `NoteEdit.goNote` (enter that note, the caret at the change; in Draft the window stays in the body).

### Numbers and display

* The mark's number is shown through the field-show contract: `LineTokens` `shows()` asks `FieldShow.fieldText` at a noteRef, which answers from `NoteNumbers.markText`, so the existing atomic-token merge makes it ONE token in the run's format. The reuse key gains `nk` (`NoteNumbers.noteKey`, `''` for most paragraphs): `ItemMake.paraItem`, `ItemReuse` `reuseKey`/`sameKey`, and `TblReuse` (items with `nk` are "listed") keep a paragraph or cell only while its marks show the same texts. A note's layout sets `L.noteId` and `L.noteLabel` (its own mark shows the number of the note's body mark).
* `numbersByPage(doc, pageOf)` serves "restart each page" (footnotes only; endnotes' `eachPage` counts as continuous): `NoteHooks.notePass` makes up to `MAX_PASSES` = 2 extra layouts per DocVersion (`ViewPass` `fieldPass` = `passOf \|\| notePass`); until they settle the previous pass's numbers show.

### Footnotes on the pages: the settle (replaces the footnote hook D36)

The per-item hook `G.reserve(frame, refs)` has been REMOVED (from `PageFill`, `PageGalley`, `Paginate` and the test fixtures): called once per item and per column frame, and again when an item is re-fitted, it could not tell which lines of a split paragraph hold the mark, could not reserve one area across the columns and double-counted. `G.notes` and the facts' `refs` (`PageGalley`, from `NoteHooks.refsOf`) take its place, and `Paginate` calls `NotePlace.settle` in place of `fillPage` when `G.notes` is set; a document with no footnote marked in its body has no `G.notes` and paginates exactly as before.

`NotePlace.settle(G, out, y0, prev)`, per page:

* The foot holds, in order, the notes passed on from the page before and the notes of the marks on this page's lines (the first mark of each note, `refsOn`), under the separator, or under the continuation separator when the first piece goes on from the page before.
* Initial placement: fill the body with frame `F - R`, `R` starting at the room the carried-in notes need (capped so the body keeps its first line). On a page with no carry and no marks this first fill is the only one: exactly `fillPage`.
* Reserve per try: when every note fits whole (in `F - used`) the solution is feasible and kept if it is the furthest so far; try `R = max(need, bad + 1)` when that is smaller. When the notes do not fit: if the body already ends with the last mark's line and the notes before it (whole) plus that note's first line and the notice fit, accept it: that note is cut, as Word does near the page bottom. Otherwise estimate the longest frame from the marks' places in this fill (either marks 0..i keep their notes whole and the frame runs up to mark i+1's line, or marks 0..i-1 are whole, mark i's note is cut and the body ends with mark i's line); if none fits, the frame ends above the first mark's line, which moves that line to the next page with its note. Set `bad = estimate - 1` and try again.
* `MAX_TRIES` = 5 fills a page bound (typically 2); the page keeps the last (furthest) FITTING solution; if none was feasible, the last fill, its notes cut where the foot ends and the rest passed on in `left`. Nothing is lost or placed twice: pages go on past the end of the galley while anything is left, and a page with no body shows at least one note line. Whole notes first: a note is cut only when its mark's line is the last body line on the page.
* `KEEP` (1e-6 px) slack: `PageFill` compares px with no epsilon, and a body frame about 2e-14 px short of its first line cut that line at its foot, leaving the pages a long note goes on over with no body. The fill is given `KEEP` more, the room is compared with the same slack, and the record gets the frame back as worked out.
* Parity blank page: a page inserted only for odd/even parity stays empty; `Paginate.blank()` carries `notes: NotePlace.passOn(prev)` (height 0, no pieces, `left` = prev's), and the page after it continues the cut note under the continuation separator.
* The reuse record: `settle` runs inside a tap that records every note it looks at across all its tries, `(id, section, layout or null)`, with every separator height and the footnote position, and stores it with the foot. A page whose fills looked at notes but shows none gets an EMPTY foot (height 0, no pieces) so that the record exists; pages that looked at no note keep the old shape, with no `notes` key. `footAlike` compares all of it (the same layout object for each note: an edited note is a new object), so `PageReuse` `alike`/`reuse`/`take` also re-work the page BEFORE a note that was edited (a note made shorter brings its mark's line back). `PageRecord` carries `notes` and `samePage` uses `sameFoot`.
* Columns: the reserve shortens every column's frame, so footnotes sit below the columns across the text width, laid out at the section's `textW`; a carried note keeps the width it was first laid out at. `PageFrames` sets the body frame height to `notes.bodyH`; `PagePaint` draws the foot (the separator rule at mid-height of its paragraph, the pieces clipped to the frame, the notice) and `ends()` (see below).
* Cost: 10,000 notes lay out and paginate in about 1.5 times the time without notes (first pass about 270 ms); a document with no footnote does no hook, no fill and no walk (tests assert the counters).

### Notes after the text: galley runs

Endnotes (and footnotes with `pos` `sectEnd`/`docEnd`) are galley-only items, not `DocLayout` items (putting them in `L.items` would put them in `L.flow`/`L.byId` and let carets, Find and Draft see paragraphs that are not in the body). `PageGalley` `G.items` is `EndGalley.mergeOf`'s list, `G.runs` exists only when there is a run, and `facts(k)` returns `it.en.facts` for a run item. The last item of a run followed by a section gets a signed `jump` in its facts (the next section's text sits where the run starts); `PageFill` and `PageFrames` skip it as they skip a band, and `PageFill` moves its `bot` by it, so a continuous section continues below the notes on the same page. The galley index of a body item differs from `L`'s after a `sectEnd` run that is not the last, so every module that crosses goes through `EndGalley.rootK`/`bodyK` or reads `G.items` at the cursor: `PlacePrint`, `AnchorPlace`, `WrapPage`, `WrapMemo`, `WrapPass`, `WrapWant`, `WrapCells`, `ColMemo`, `ColPass`, `ColAhead`, `PrintFrags` (`fragsOf(L, pg, runs)`), `PageFind` (`placeOf` compared a galley index with a body index and gave line 0 after a run: fixed), `LineNumbers` (notes' lines are not counted). `PageReuse` uses `EndGalley.reuseRange(G, prevG)`. Only Print layout's galley (`PageHF.printGalley`, which adds `endHooks` and `noteHooks`) has runs; `PrintFrags` leaves note frags out, so the caret, hits and selection never see them (a click in the notes area gives a body position).

### Other existing modules

* `ReadPara`/`WritePara`/`ReadBody`/`TblRead`/`StoryRead`: marks, the `notes` flags, and `StoryRead` exports `strictRoot`, `hasSectPr`, `readBlocks` for `NoteRead`. `DocxRead`/`DocxWrite`/`WriteParts`: the notes parts are read, written (`NoteWrite.notesOut`), given their content type when new, and checked. `NewDoc` gets `notes` and `meta.noteParts`. `Info` counts `noteRef` marks as footnotes and endnotes.
* `Walk`: `scanStories` also walks `doc.notes` (footnotes then endnotes); more ids are reserved and note fonts are listed by `Info`.
* `Clip*`: the slice has `notes: [{kind, id, note}]` ONLY when its blocks hold a mark whose note the document has as a normal note (then the styles, table styles and lists are worked out over the body blocks and the note blocks); `ClipStore` keeps it by reference; HTML and plain routes never have it. `ClipPaste` runs `ClipNotes.carry` after `deleteRange` and `fitDepth`, in the paste's `d.atomic`: every mark gets a new id (`nextNoteId` taken NOW and one more each, so a pasted mark never names an existing note) and a NEW Note with fresh block ids; two marks of one note get a copy each; a mark whose note was not carried is dropped silently. `ClipClean` has an `inNote` option (its own mark kept, any other mark dropped) and a `toNote` option (`ClipPaste` sets it when `d` is a note's facade): a note's own mark (`self`) pasted in the same document is kept only in a note, never in the body or a header (Word writes `w:footnoteRef` only in a note); another document gets Word's note styles by name first (`ClipNotes.styleUp`). Pictures and links in a carried note are kept within a document (fresh `docPr` ids, `ClipPics` `docPrIds` exported) and dropped in another (the media is related from the notes part; carrying it needs that part's `.rels`: not done). `ClipRoute` passes a `report` and beeps ("The footnotes or endnotes of this document could not be read: the text was pasted without its note marks." for a kept-as-bytes kind). The old `ClipClean` stopgap that dropped a cut mark pasted back was removed.
* `WordCount`/`CountBox`/`WordChoices`: `count(doc, sel, L, opts)` / `countView(v, opts)` with `opts.notes` (default false: `TestHook` and old callers unchanged); the box has "Include footnotes and endnotes" (default on, kept as `countNotes` in `Choices:Letters`). Whole document: `NotePick.noteList` (each normal note once, in mark order); a selection: the notes whose marks lie in the covered paragraphs (tables inside too). Note blocks are counted like body blocks under the shared 1e6 node budget. The note's own mark and a custom mark's text are not counted; the space after the own mark is (to check in real Word). In header, footer and note mode, notes are not counted. `NUMWORDS` counts the body only (an assumption to check). 10,000 notes: 2.8 ms on against 1.1 ms off.
* `Keymap`/`KeymapMore`/`DocKeys`/`EditKeys`: `Keymap` understands `Alt+` (canonical `Ctrl+Alt+Shift+K`); with Alt held only rows naming Alt match, the letter taken from `domEvent.code` when present (Option on a Mac and AltGr change the character). Rows: `footnote` Ctrl+Alt+F, `endnote` Ctrl+Alt+D, `nextNote` Alt+Down, `prevNote` Alt+Up (the WINDOW ids). `EditKeys` sends Alt keys to the keymap before the movement keys; a key the command does not use (Alt+Down outside the mode) goes on. `MacKeys` does not map Cmd with Alt: on a Mac the keys are Ctrl+Option (the `KeymapMore` header says "Ctrl on a Mac too, with Option as Alt"). This is read from the code and has not been tried in a real Mac browser (wimp.js hands Ctrl+Alt with a non-letter key to text input); the menu items always work.
* `HdrMode`/`HdrStep`/`ViewMenu`/`WinMenu`/`InsertMenu`/`TabsBox`: the notes mode reuses the header mode slot (`view.hdr`, kind `'note'`), so Escape (`v.leaveHdr`), `setView`, `FieldUpdate`, the info line and the section boxes' refusals work unchanged; the header-specific readers check the kind (WinMenu shows Footnote/Endnote in the notes mode, ViewMenu's Header and footer item is ticked and its options shaded only in the header mode, `HdrMode.toggle` from the notes mode enters the header). `InsertMenu` gets `NoteMenu.noteItems` after Bookmark.... `TabsBox` `IN_HDR` now reads "Leave the header or footer, or the note, first (Escape): ...". `AppWin` calls `attachNotes`.
* `StylesBuiltin`: Footnote Text, Footnote Reference, Endnote Text and Endnote Reference are available through `builtinStyle` only (not in `ensureBuiltins`/`galleryIds`); `NoteStyle` makes them on first use.
* `Document`: `NoteKeep` at the end of each outermost group (above). `DocVersion` bumps on every note op, undo and redo.

### The corpus, the hand-off files and the numbers

* `note-roundtrip.test.mjs` and `noteref-corpus.test.mjs`: every corpus note part written back byte for byte, and every part of a file written with marks modelled equals the file written with `noteMarks: false`. `notes-roundtrip.test.mjs` (`WORD_EDIT_CORPUS=1` for all files): the pipeline (deep-frozen Doc through layout, galley and pages, then save: every part as a save without layout, notes parts as read, every `w:footnoteReference`/`w:endnoteReference` element as it was), the commands story, 40-command seeded bursts, the census, hostile files, the layout oracle and page starts. With the 16 hand-off files in the corpus folder: 191 files with a notes part opened, laid out and saved unchanged (369 notes parts, 253 marks, 1284 pages); census footnotes 213 marks (0 missing, 4 orphans, 0 twice, 0 number differences), endnotes 38 marks (1 orphan); story 191/191; bursts over 808 files, 787 run and 21 refused by the reader, 0 failures. Page starts: `pages-corpus` is pinned at 2277 pages and 325 of 1387 matched (before notes were laid out, 323); of the 8 files with Word's starts and notes, 48 of 235 matched without notes on the pages and 50 with. Orphans in the corpus (5 notes in 2 files) have their marks in raw content (text boxes, hyperlinks); they are kept and written back.
* The hand-off builder is `node tests/moreapps/handoff-notes.mjs`: it writes `en-1`..`en-16` `.docx` and `en-README.txt` (questions EN1..EN16, a priority list) into the git-ignored `tests/moreapps/corpus/handoff/`: en-1 (new document, 3 footnotes and 2 endnotes made by the commands), en-2 one footnote, en-3 20 footnotes restarting each page, en-4 a 46-paragraph footnote, en-5 endnotes at the end of the document, en-6 at each section's end, en-7 one section per number format, en-8 start at 5, en-9 restart each section, en-10 bold, a list and a table in a note, en-11 custom marks, en-12 swap, en-13 below text, en-14 notes in table cells, en-15 and en-16 Word-shaped documents with a note added and a mark deleted. They have NOT yet been opened in real Word.
* `word-notes.mjs` is the desktop test (Ctrl+Alt+F, the mode, Escape, Alt+Down/Up, double-clicks, delete and undo, cut and paste, Convert, Custom mark, Word count).

### Tests

```
node --test tests/moreapps/note-roundtrip.test.mjs tests/moreapps/noteref.test.mjs tests/moreapps/noteref-corpus.test.mjs tests/moreapps/noteopts.test.mjs tests/moreapps/notenumbers.test.mjs   # the model, reader, writer, numbers
node --test tests/moreapps/notelayout.test.mjs tests/moreapps/notepages.test.mjs tests/moreapps/endnotes-layout.test.mjs tests/moreapps/endnotes-wrap.test.mjs   # notes on the pages
node --test tests/moreapps/opsnotes.test.mjs tests/moreapps/storyfacade.test.mjs tests/moreapps/notecmd.test.mjs tests/moreapps/noteedit.test.mjs tests/moreapps/clipnotes.test.mjs tests/moreapps/noteconvert.test.mjs tests/moreapps/notepatch.test.mjs   # ops, facade, commands, the mode, clipboard
node --test tests/moreapps/notes-roundtrip.test.mjs   # the pipeline, story, bursts, census, hostile files, layout oracle (WORD_EDIT_CORPUS=1: every corpus file, about 5 minutes)
node tests/moreapps/word-notes.mjs   # browser: the notes mode, cut and paste, Convert, Custom mark
node tests/moreapps/handoff-notes.mjs   # writes en-1..en-16 .docx and en-README.txt (local, git-ignored)
```

### Known limits and questions

* Endnotes' default number format: `NoteOpts.DEFAULTS` gives `decimal`, but Word's own default for endnotes may be i, ii, iii. Two Word files in the corpus write `w:numFmt decimal` for their endnotes (settings and sectPr) while 12 Word files with endnotes write none. If Word's default is lower Roman, !Letters shows 1, 2 where Word shows i, ii, and `NotePatch` never writes `decimal` for a user who picks 1, 2, 3 (it equals our default). Not changed (EN16, priority 7). The fix is `endnotes.numFmt 'lowerRoman'` in `NoteOpts.DEFAULTS` and the endnote tests.
* Marks inside tracked insertions, hyperlinks and content controls stay raw (2 of 179 marks in the corpus), so later numbers can differ from Word's; marks and notes in headers, footers and text boxes are raw; pictures in notes are kept, not shown; Find from the body does not search notes; no cross-references to notes (Batch E3); notes with links or pictures are not converted (`rels`); a list in a note carried to another document gets its own list definition.
* Endnotes continued onto another page have no continuation separator or notice (Word has one); notes are not wrapped round floating pictures (a float anchored on the run's page may sit over the notes); in a section with unequal columns endnotes use the first column's width; the section break mark of a section followed by a run is drawn under its last paragraph, before the notes; a `keepNext` chain crossing a `jump` is measured approximately; `vShift` (vAlign) leaves the foot out and the foot is not moved down with the body under `beneathText` plus vAlign.
* A note longer than a page is edited where it starts (the caret on its later lines is drawn below the first piece). Undo of a note edit in Draft stays in the body. No double-click on the note's own number to go to the mark (Escape is the way back). A mark naming a continuation separator (id 0) in a hostile file is numbered. A note's bookmark names can repeat the body's. The bookmark in a note and `storyMarks` (which walks `doc.stories` only) are not unified for goTo.
* To check in real Word: the notes part and separators made for the first note; how a custom mark is written (the text as the note's first run, in the reference style, not `w:footnoteRef`) and the 10-character limit and which characters Word refuses; the style switch on Convert and Word's ids on save (we take max + 1); the endnote number format (EN16); notes in columns placed across the page width (Word may put them in the column holding the mark); the body keeping one line a page that a long note goes on over (EN6); a footnote kept whole when it fits and cut only at its mark's line; the separator sizes (2 inches, 1 px; the continuation separator the text width, mid-height of its paragraph); the symbol sequence (* dagger double dagger section sign, then doubled and tripled); `sectEnd`/`docEnd` footnotes shown as flowing notes under the footnote separator; the Word count with notes (the space after the own mark counted; NUMWORDS body only); and that Whole document clears per-section overrides. Ctrl+Alt+F/D and Alt+Down/Up need the browser to deliver Alt (Playwright does; a Mac's Option is mapped by `domEvent.code`; on some systems Ctrl+Alt is AltGr; the menu items always work).

## Tables of contents, captions, cross-references and field update (Batch E3): what changed

The new modules are in the table of "The application modules" above (rows `BookmarkIndex` to `XrefTargets,
XrefCmd, XrefBox`). This section is the rules that cut across them. User guide: `$.Docs.Letters` part 25.

* **Nothing updates by itself.** Opening, typing, saving, printing and changing the view never change a stored
  result. Fields are updated only by Edit > Update field, Edit > Update all fields, the TOC box's Update, Insert >
  Caption..., and Insert > Cross-reference... (which fills its own result). `w:dirty` is read and ignored on open
  (saved unchanged) and cleared on update.
* **A real TOC field.** The result is Word's: entry paragraphs in `TOC n`, each a `w:hyperlink w:anchor` (with `\h`),
  the text, a tab and a PAGEREF field (a structural-equality test compares a generated entry to a real
  `Complex01.docx` one); the field begin and code in the first entry paragraph, the end in a paragraph of its own.
  Hidden `_Toc` + 9 digits bookmarks on the headings (reused when a bookmark already spans the heading) and `_Ref` +
  9 digits for cross-references are added in the same step; their ids come from `Bookmarks.nextBookmarkId`, the one
  chooser all bookmark writers share (bodies, stories, notes). A new document's styles part has none of TOC 1-9, TOC
  Heading, Hyperlink, Caption, Table of Figures: they are latent in `StylesBuiltin` (`builtinStyle`, not in
  `builtins()`), added by `StyleCmd.ensureBuiltin` on first use.
* **The update order and the bound.** `FieldPasses.STEPS` is facts, seq, chapters, refs, fields, toc, pages. The
  document is laid out again between passes (`ctx.relayout`: `ViewPass.settle` in a window, a stub in tests) while a
  paged step changed a result, `MAX_PASSES` = 3 passes in all. A table of contents moves its own headings, so
  pass 1 builds it with the old pages, pass 2 on the new, pass 3 finds nothing to change (tested with a one-line
  stored result over 70 headings each on its own page); a document that still moves says 'Pages not settled after
  3 passes.'. A second run makes no change and no undo step.
* **Body only.** `FieldPasses.run` on the body is the body (Word's Ctrl+A F9). Headers, footers and notes are
  updated through their `StoryFacade` by Edit > Update field in that mode (Update all fields is shaded there). A REF
  or NOTEREF typed inside a note is therefore refreshed only in the notes mode.
* **A table inserted in Outline or Web layout has no page numbers** (`updateCtx` gives no pages there): the entries are made without them; Print layout and Update field (page numbers only) or Update all fields fill them. A document with dozens of tables of contents is slow to update (each is rebuilt on every pass, up to `MAX_PASSES`).
